News.title: Ghoulish content creators slammed for visiting Lindsay Clancy’s home where she killed kids after jury’s secretive trip
News.content:
TRUE crime sleuths have sparked outrage by filming drive-by videos of the former home where Lindsay Clancy killed her three children — just days after jurors were given a rare tour of the property.

Clancy is accused of murdering five-year-old daughter Cora, three-year-old son Dawson and eight-month-old son Callan at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023.



Prosecutors allege Clancy strangled the children with exercise bands and left them in the basement of the home, while her husband, Patrick, was out picking up dinner.

She then allegedly attempted to take her own life by jumping from a second-floor window.





The former labor and delivery nurse survived the fall and has been left paralyzed from the waist down.

Clancy, 35, has pleaded not guilty to murder and other charges, with her defense arguing that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time and had been prescribed a cocktail of medications.

Jurors were taken to the home to see the layout for themselves and better understand the physical evidence and competing accounts of what happened inside on the night of the killings.

Following the tragedy, Patrick sold the residence in January 2024 for $675,000.



Social media footage obtained by The U.S. Sun shows content creators filming the home while driving past and later sharing the videos on Instagram and TikTok.

One user, named Jamies Just Jammin, wrote, “I debated whether or not I should post this here as this is not what my page is about, but where the entire nation is obsessed with this case I thought some may be interested.

“The Clancy murders happened less than 20 minutes from where I live. I had to go into the town recently for something and drove by the Clancy house. I said a prayer for Cora, Dawson, and Callan.”

But she was slammed by followers on Instagram who felt it was inappropriate.

One wrote underneath, “Ok and? I live 5 min away. Not putting someone’s home on social media though.”



A second wrote, “I dont think driving by the house was necessary..a pix would have been fine.”

“I get everyone’s obsession with this. I am too. My parents live on this side of town and it’s been crazy. A couple bought the house. Probably best to let them have privacy. I can’t imagine living there now,” a third added.

One also told the user to “get a life,” while others were glad to see the footage and admitted they were also “obsessed” with the case.



The female creator wrote back, “There is a whole country very interested in this case, Kristine. Should they ‘get a life’ too? Or are you bigger than everyone?”

Jamie, who posted the video, also claimed she could still see the playground in the backyard at the home.

One follower admitted, “I drove by myself recently. I just had to. It was so heartbreaking seeing where it all happened.”

The creator also shared the clip on TikTok where it was liked by more than 12,000 users.

Another content creator, who goes by @CourtDawgDaniel, has been parking his RV at the courthouse every day and confronting people as they come and go from the trial.



He filmed himself driving the route from the courthouse to the Clancy home earlier this week, before posting the footage on social media.

“We are about to make a turn onto the street the Clancy’s lived on,” Daniel is heard saying in the clip.

“It’s about point one miles up the road on the left, obviously I’m not going to divulge the address online, you know, for privacy concerns for the people that live there now, but I’ll try to drive real slow.”

“Got a bunch of cars behind me, but want to make sure we get a good look at this house. This is it right here,” he added, as the camera panned across.

He then filmed the property, with a boat visible beneath a cover in the driveway, and shared the video on TikTok and Instagram.



One user wrote underneath, “How twisted a guy are you. Get the hell out of their it’s none of ours business old man (sic).”

A third TikToker also posted a video driving down the street and past the house, writing, “3 min. drive from Clancy house to CVS.”

The video was liked by more than 55,000 people, with many debating the case in the comments.

The U.S. Sun has reached out to the new owners of the home.

Other social media users have shared the full address of the property from public court records.



The U.S. Sun obtained filings that show the buyers – a practicing attorney operating out of Plymouth, Massachusetts, alongside another co-owner – acquired the home before subsequently moving the property title into a personal living trust for estate planning.

They also financed the purchase by taking out a $607,500 mortgage through CMG Mortgage INC.

Ahead of Clancy’s murder trial, prosecutors filed a motion requesting a formal jury tour of the private residence.

The prosecution argued that physically seeing the home’s layout was vital for jurors to understand the spatial context of the crime, including the distance between the basement, the main floor, and the second-floor window.

The current homeowners objected and asked the court to block the visit.



However, the judge ultimately overruled them, deciding that the physical context of the home provided necessary evidence for the jury to evaluate the case.

In late July, court officers and police supervised a controlled walk-through where jurors inspected the basement, main living areas, and upper level.

Strict court rules were enforced prohibiting anyone from opening closet doors, touching personal property, or disturbing items inside the house.

Some social media users following the trial have been left stunned that the Clancy family home is still standing, after other properties linked to notorious murder cases have been demolished.

The off-campus home where four University of Idaho students were murdered by Bryan Kohberger was torn down before his trial began.



One Facebook user in a Clancy trial group wrote: “I just can’t understand how anyone could live in this house after what happened there. While I can understand selling it from the father’s POV, finances etc. I just can’t imagine living there.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another said the property should have been demolished and turned into “a memorial or a park/playground in memory of the children.”

A third added, “I could never live there after those babies died. I’d cry and it would break my heart. God bless those people who bought it.”

News.title: Mystery of warship which vanished 118 years ago is finally solved as divers find it off UK coast
News.content:
SEA SOLVE Mystery of warship which vanished 118 years ago is finally solved as divers find it off UK coast

DIVERS have discovered the long-lost wreck of a Royal Navy warship which sank 118 years ago.

HMS Tiger disappeared in 1908, after she strayed into the path of the 10,000-ton HMS Berwick during a training exercise and was sliced in two.



Fewer than half of its 57 crew members survived the deadly collision, which took place just off the Isle of Wight.

For over a century, the exact coordinates of the wreckage have remained a mystery to divers – until today.



Shipwreck historians from ProjectXplore have now discovered the remains of the sunken torpedo destroyer – just as new legislation comes into effect to protect wreckages.

Under the Armed Forces Bill, it will now be an offence to disturb or dislodge items from a wreck without permission.





Divers will be permitted to visit the sites, under a ‘look but don’t touch’ policy.

Automatic legal protections will apply to thousands of graves belonging to sailors and marines.

Minister for the Armed Forces Louise Sandher-Jones MP said: “As well as protecting UK national security, Defence has a role to play in preserving our maritime heritage and the memory of those who gave their lives serving their country.”

She added that the new measures will give sailors who died at sea the “dignity and respect they deserve”.



While dozens of military shipwrecks have been safeguarded from illegal activity since the mid-1980s, only vessels lost within the last 200 years can qualify for protection.

Expanding the Protection of Military Remains Act will ensure wreckages dating as far back as the Spanish Armada – including those of the former enemy – will be protected.



Employees at ProjectXplore – who spent years figuring out the location of HMS Tiger through intensive archival research – have welcomed the amendments.

Leo Fielding and Dan McMullen, co-organisers of ProjectXplore said: “It has been the privilege of a lifetime to research, discover and document the wreck of HMS Tiger.

“We sincerely hope that our work will ensure that HMS Tiger, her story and the memory of those connected with her endure for future generations.

“ProjectXplore welcomes the proposed amendments in the Armed Forces Bill.

“We believe they represent a constructive step forward in protecting the United Kingdom’s maritime heritage and ensuring that wreck sites of historical and archaeological significance are appropriately safeguarded.”



Royal Navy Deputy Fleet Wreck Officer Lieutenant Commander Jen Smith added: “Protecting military wrecks helps to ensure they are preserved for future generations.

“This is beneficial for our rich maritime heritage and the diving community who keep the stories of our lost shipwrecks alive.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It follows the discovery of an even older vessel in June last year, off the coast of Plymouth.

SS Nantes sank in 1888 after colliding with a German sailing vessel, sinking approximately ten hours after the hit as desperate crew members plugged the holes with mattresses.

News.title: China evacuates ONE MILLION people as Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall bringing 100mph gales and grounding 1,000 flights
News.content:
CHINA has evacuated more than one million people as Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall, bringing devastation with it.

Several provinces in the east of the country have been hit by torrential rain and storms with around 100mph gales, stopping 40 per cent of flights.



Dolphin, China’s most powerful typhoon so far this year, packed maximum sustained winds of 151kph (93.8mph) near its centre when it made landfall in Zhejiang, the province to the south and west of Shanghai, on Sunday evening before weakening to a tropical storm.

Its remaining rain clouds continued to soak the eastern provinces including Anhui, Jiangsu and Shandong on Monday.



Many streets in Shanghai, the country’s second most populous city, were flooded, including in the main commercial centres.

The city’s two airports cancelled a total of 943 flights due to the typhoon, reducing capacity by nearly 40 per cent, state broadcaster CCTV said.



China Eastern Airlines said on Monday it was trying to resume flights to Shanghai, Zhejiang and other destinations in an “orderly manner.”

Shanghai also suspended some of its metro lines on Monday, and China Railway Chengdu Group suspended 115 trains, state news agency Xinhua reported.



Many streets in Shanghai’s suburban Jiading and Qingpu districts around the city centre remained waterlogged, according to live-streams shared by residents on social media.

The live videos showed people wading through knee-high murky water.

Hou Lina, 38, who works in sales in Jiading in Shanghai said: “It rained almost all-night last night.



“When I woke up this morning, I found the neighbourhood flooded, and the streets were severely flooded.”

She added: “I’ve lived in Shanghai for 10 years, and this is the first time I’ve experienced such inconvenience from a typhoon.

“This is the first time I’ve encountered such widespread flooding.”



In Shanghai’s Jinshan, the district authority said non-essential businesses and organisations could temporarily halt operations, classes, outdoor events and transit services, amid forecasts of continued strong winds and heavy rain on Monday.

Authorities warned of risks of severe flooding and landslides in some areas.

State broadcaster CCTV reported that authorities in Yueqing, a city in Zhejiang province, searched for people trapped in flooded homes.

Powerful winds and lashing rain flipped over a truck in Zhejiang’s Wenzhou, a video posted on TikTok on Sunday showed.

It was not clear what happened to the driver.



Authorities warned that 74 rivers in the Taihu Lake basin and the coastal areas of eastern Zhejiang have exceeded warning levels, and that flood risks for small and medium-sized rivers in heavy rainfall areas are high.

Dolphin is forecast to move deeper inland to the central provinces of Hubei and Henan in the coming days while also pushing moisture north.

Authorities in the capital Beijing raised warnings for torrential rain and said the city was prepared to activate its flood control response on Tuesday morning.

Beijing is expected to experience “significant rainfall” from Tuesday until Thursday, with authorities warning of the risk of flash floods in the city and landslides in the surrounding mountainous areas.

The typhoon had already travelled 3,728 miles before it made landfall, giving it a life-cycle three times longer than an ordinary typhoon, and bringing with it an ultra-large cloud system that enveloped China’s east, CCTV said in another report.



Dolphin’s impact was also being compared to Doksuri in 2023.

That typhoon crossed the country after causing destruction in southeastern Fujian province, unleashing record-breaking rainfall in Beijing.

As the storm clouds meet colder air in the north, Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei will need to brace for heavy rain into Thursday, CCTV said.

Hong Kong, on China’s southern coast, has seen extreme heat due to Dolphin, recording its hottest day ever on Sunday at 36.9C, the highest since records began in 1884, according to the Hong Kong Observatory, the territory’s weather body.

TSR (Tropical Storm Risk) said it expected the 2026 northwest Pacific typhoon season to be one of the most active on record and to include 28 tropical storms, 20 typhoons and 13 intense typhoons.



TSR said the ongoing strong El Nino event, high activity to date and weaker-than-normal trade winds across the northwest Pacific basin, were key reasons for the intensity of the typhoon season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Elsewhere, Tropical Storm Chan-hom was heading toward Japan’s Pacific coast.

The storm had 51 mph winds on Monday morning and was forecast to strengthen slightly before landfall Tuesday into Wednesday, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

News.title: Cops dig up church car park after tip-off in cold case of missing mum-of-two who vanished 34 years ago
News.content:
FRESH SEARCH Cops dig up church car park after tip-off in cold case of missing mum-of-two who vanished 34 years ago

COPS investigating the disappearance of a mum-of-two who went missing 34 years ago have dug up a car park in search of clues.

Patricia Hall, then aged 39, vanished on January 25, 1992, during a family day out in Ripon, North Yorkshire.



West Yorkshire Police have started digging near Moravian Church in Fulneck, Leeds, after the team received reports of new “information” about Patricia’s disappearance.

However, “nothing of note” has yet been found, cops said today.



Police have released images of the site, with workers pictured standing next to several large black bags.

Although detectives have not yet recovered a body, an inquest into her death was launched in April this year at Wakefield Coroner’s Court.





Coroner Oliver Longstaff explained how Patricia’s sister, Christine Weatherhead, had requested a new application to hold an inquest.

Patricia’s husband Keith was previously tried for murder – after reports of their tumultuous marriage emerged – but was found not guilty in 1994.

In a disturbing interview with an undercover cop, Keith claimed to have killed his wife – but the jury was never allowed to hear the recorded “admission”.

He later backtracked and said that he had only confessed to killing her to please his new girlfriend – the undercover cop – in a bid to convince her Patricia wasn’t coming back and they could continue their relationship.

In a police interview, Keith said: “When I left that car, I was going to go back and say, ‘You know what I said is a load of ooish, don’t you? Made up entirely to please you?’ And I should have done, really.”



The inquest heard how there had been no sightings of her since her disappearance and no “circumstantial evidence” to suggest she was still alive – such as use of a bank account or contact with family.

Cops stated that the car park dig is purely speculative, as the team attempts to recover information.

A spokesperson said: “Officers from West Yorkshire Police’s Major Investigation Review Team are currently examining a site at Fulneck, Pudsey, in connection with the disappearance of Patricia Hall in Leeds in 1992.

“The search for potential evidence follows recent information received by the team and is being carried out on a speculative basis.

“There is nothing to suggest any link to the Moravian Church, which owns the site.”



Assistant Chief Constable Sarah Jones said Patricia Hall’s family had been informed about the latest developments.

She said: “We are conscious of the understandable public focus that this activity is likely to attract in this high-profile case.

“Patricia’s family have been informed, and we will be keeping them updated.

“We obviously have a duty to act on any new information we receive but at this stage we are keeping an open mind.”

“The Major Investigation Review Team carried out a thorough cold case review into Patricia’s disappearance which concluded last year without establishing any new lines of enquiry.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She added that the team would welcome any new or additional information that could assist the inquiry.

News.title: Chaos on major motorway as lorry fire shuts lanes and drivers stuck in hour-long delays
News.content:
A LORRY has caught fire on a major motorway causing traffic to grind to a halt.

The M25 has been closed off in the anticlockwise direction between J6 and J5 in Kent.

Hour-long delays are expected and tailbacks are said to have reached J8.

Local lanes are also reportedly experiencing congestion as motorists reroute.





A fire brigade has been called to the scene and is currently tackling the blaze, with smoke seen rising across the M25.

Images show three fire engines parked across the lanes by J5, with thick traffic pictured behind.

The fire is understood to be located in the cargo hold of the lorry.

It follows another closure on the M23 in Surrey in the northbound direction between J9 and J9a this afternoon.

Emergency services were called to tackle a van fire.

Delays of more than 10 minutes and one mile of congestion were reported.

News.title: Australian PM accused of ‘crude joke’ about Japan’s female leader’s ‘melons’ as diplomatic row erupts
News.content:
THE Australian PM has been accused of making a crude joke about the Japanese leader’s “melons” – sparking a furious diplomatic row.

Anthony Albanese was appearing on the Bush Deep podcast when he was asked about the worst gift he had received while overseas.



After briefly pausing, he said he had recently received a gift that was “pretty strange but ended up being quite good”.

The gift was two royal melons given to him by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during an official visit in May.



During the podcast, host Nikki Osbourne asked Mr Albanese how Ms Takaichi had managed to “smuggle” the melons through Australian customs.

The Australian comedian then made a suggestive gesture with both hands in front of her chest.

Mr Albanese quickly mimicked the gesture before joking that Ms Takaichi had brought “a couple of melons… as you do”.

Later in the podcast, Osbourne made the startling observation that the Japanese leader had “come in looking like Pamela Anderson“.



Mr Albanese did not object to the comment.

The clip has since sparked outrage in Japan, with former Australian ambassador to Japan Shingo Yamagami penning a scathing opinion piece.

Yamagami, who served as Japan’s ambassador to Australia from 2020 to 2023, said Mr Albanese’s comments were “not only ungracious” but betrayed “the close bonds of our two nations”.

He described the comments and gestures as “appalling” and criticised the Prime Minister for failing to show proper respect for the gift.

“A crown melon is the most prized fruit in Japan and treasured as something special,” he said.



Mr Albanese has also faced criticism from opposition politicians, who branded his comments “grubby” and “beneath the office of prime minister”.

Opposition leader Angus Taylor said: “They were insulting and the prime minister should make a personal apology.”

But senior cabinet ministers have rushed to his defence.

Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek said: “Japan is a very important strategic and economic partner … and I think the former ambassador is wrong in his interpretation.”

Health Minister Mark Butler also stressed Australia’s close economic and security ties with Japan.



He said: “It’s very close. It involves constant communication between our two countries, two at the highest level.

“I know Prime Minister Albanese feels the deepest respect for that relationship.”

It is not the first time Mr Albanese has found himself at the centre of controversy over comments made on a podcast.

During the same episode, Osbourne asked him whom he would “shag, marry and date” between Australian icons Kylie Minogue, Nicole Kidman and Rhonda Burchmore.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

After initially hesitating, the Prime Minister gave the crude response: Minogue “for all of the above”.



He later issued a one-line apology, saying he was “unequivocally” sorry for the incident.

News.title: Schoolgirl, 11, who died in water near Scots beauty spot is named by cops
News.content:
A SCHOOLGIRL who tragically died after being found in a river near a Scots beauty spot has been named by cops.

Emergency services raced to the scene at Gore Glen Woodland Park in Midlothian on Friday afternoon after the young girl was reported missing.



The alarm was raised after police received reports of concerns for 11-year-old Faith Curran in the area around 12.40pm.

A major search and rescue operation was launched to find the girl, but devastatingly, her body was found in Gore Water close to Shank Bridge near the village of Gorebridge around 4.25pm.



She was pronounced dead at the scene.

Faith’s heartbroken family has paid tribute to their “happy, adventurous, and outgoing girl who enjoyed life” through Police Scotland.

They also thanked everyone who assisted them with their search and for their support and kindness.

And they have asked that their privacy is respected during this difficult time.

Police say the girl’s death is currently being treated as “unexplained”, however, there are not believed to be suspicious circumstances.

An investigation is currently underway to find out the full circumstances surrounding the tragedy.



Floral tributes have been left at the bridge after the incident last weekend.

A section of woodland near the water where her body was found had been taped off by cops.

A neighbour in the nearby Arniston estate previously told The Scottish Sun: “It’s absolutely tragic. I can’t stop thinking about it.

“Everyone I’ve spoken to is just so upset and shocked. I’ve barely slept for thinking about it.”



Another neighbour said he woke up to the news on Saturday morning.

He said: “I didn’t know a thing about it until I seen it on social media. Your heart just breaks for the family. How do you ever get over that?”

Another local added: “That’s a popular wee trail for dog walkers and the like. It’s just so tragic.”

A statement from the force read: “The 11-year-old girl who died following an incident in the Gore Glen area, near Gorebridge, can be named as Faith Curran.



“Faith’s family reported her missing in the area around 12.40pm on Thursday, 6 August, 2026.

“Her body was found in the Gore Water near to Shanks Bridge around 4.25pm.

“She was pronounced dead at the scene and her family are aware. They have asked that their privacy is respected.

“Faith’s family would like to thank those who assisted them with their search, for their support and kindness.

“They describe Faith as a ‘happy, adventurous, and outgoing girl who enjoyed life’.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The death is being treated as unexplained however there are not believed to be suspicious circumstances.

“Enquiries remain ongoing and a report will be sent to the Procurator Fiscal in due course.”

News.title: Child’s body found at house as man, 31, and woman, 32, charged with preventing lawful burial
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC FIND Child’s body found at house as man, 31, and woman, 32, charged with preventing lawful burial

A 31-YEAR-OLD man and a woman, aged 32, have been charged with preventing a lawful burial after a child’s body was found at a house.

Cops discovered the body at a property in Southend, Essex, on August 7, following a welfare concern raised by social services.

Sophie Dean, 31, of Coates House, Kenway, Southend, and James Thorpe, 32, of Frobisher Way, Shoeburyness, have been charged with preventing a lawful and decent burial of a dead body.

The charge relates to a time period between July 3, 2025 and August 6, 2026.





Mr Thorpe has also been charged with obstruction of a constable in the execution of their duty, said Essex Police.

Both appeared at Southend Magistrates’ Court on August 10 and were remanded in custody.

The pair are due to appear next at Basildon Crown Court on September 7, cops added.

An Essex Police spokesperson said: “The investigation into the child’s death will continue to be led by detectives from our Crime and Public Protection Command.



“We would also encourage anyone with information that could assist us and who has not yet spoken to us to please come forward and do so, quoting investigation number 42/125225/26.”

No further details about the child or the circumstances of their death have been released.

News.title: More than two-thirds of England now in drought
News.content:
Last month, England and Wales saw the driest July since records began in 1836 - while for southern England, it was the driest month ever recorded.

South-east England received 1% of the expected average rainfall for July, while some parts of Hampshire, Isle of Wight and West Sussex have not had a rain day for 59 days.

All of England is experiencing pressure on water resources, the National Drought Group said.

Farmers have reported reduced output after their earliest harvests in 20 years, with the National Farmers Union (NFU) warning that continued dry weather could lead to some food shortages.

NFU president Tom Bradshaw said yields of wheat and oats were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they have been unable to grow grass.

Water Minister Emma Hardy said the government is working to make it easier for farmers to build more on-site irrigation reservoirs, which capture and hold water.

Only 14% of England's rivers are considered to be at normal levels, while 22% are "exceptionally low" - including the River Avon in south-west England and the River Ely Ouse in eastern England.

The Environment Agency has warned that low water levels have resulted in potential navigation issues for boats on the Thames, Lark and Ouse.

Reservoir levels have also continued to decline, with almost all across England below normal and five classed as "exceptionally low", according to the agency.

Warmer water is putting fish under "severe stress," Head of Fisheries at the Angling Trust Mark Owen said, as it holds less dissolved oxygen.

Emma Pinchbeck, chief executive of the Climate Change Committee, said the UK is "not prepared at all" for the prolonged dry weather.

"We're seeing right now with the impacts on farming from this drought and the extreme heat we're experiencing, our infrastructure, our agricultural sector and lots of areas of the economy are not really ready for the weather we now have and how that weather will change up to 2050," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

News.title: 30 years later, a former rival will stand trial for Tupac's murder
News.content:
It was ultimately the death of another legendary rapper that helped unravel Tupac's shooting death.

Months after Shakur was gunned down, Biggie Smalls or the Notorious BIG, was killed in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles.

Both rappers were the stars of their respective rival record labels - Shakur with Death Row Records and Biggie with Bad Boy Records.

Biggie's case has remained unsolved, with no arrests or suspects.

In the mid 2000's the Los Angeles Police Department reopened the investigation and spoke with Davis, who was at a party with Biggie before the fatal shooting. While Davis said he didn't have information about Biggie's death, he did have knowledge in Tupac's case and shared that he was in the car when the rapper was shot and killed. He told police the information in exchange that he not be charged.

That deal stuck until years later, when Davis went public with his knowledge.

He co-authored a memoir in 2019 titled Compton Street Legend, that claimed he not only was inside the vehicle when Tupac was shot but also he was the person who "tossed" the gun used to kill him into the backseat of the Cadillac. He never claimed to be the person who opened fire.

Davis also elaborated on the shooting to the media, detailing information to reporters in interviews.

Las Vegas police said his public statements had "reinvigorated" the investigation. Over the next couple of years they spent time corroborating Davis' account and then in 2023, searched his home and seized multiple computers, two tubs of photographs and a slew of Tupac-related material, including a Vibe magazine.

He was arrested later that year.

Prosecutors have alleged that Tupac's killing was in retaliation for the beating of Davis' nephew - Orlando Anderson - just hours before the shooting.

They claim that Davis was the architect of the crime, who ordered the shooting and supplied the deadly weapon to further gang criminal conduct.

Nevada prosecutors argued that by publicly talking about what happened on the night of Tupac's death and writing a book where he claimed to have supplied the gun, Davis had broken the agreement he entered with law enforcement. A judge later sided with the prosecutor's argument, opening the door for Davis's arrest.

Davis and his defence team have argued that the book was co-authored and sections were embellished or fictionalised to make a profit, and they should not be viewed as direct admissions. In an interview last week with a local TV news station, Davis denied being in Las Vegas when Tupac was killed and distanced himself from the memoir that lists him as an author.

"I did not write that book," Davis told Fox 5. "A ghost writer wrote that."

He also said he might take the stand and testify at his trial. "If I have to, I will."

"This is what makes this case so fascinating. The two biggest pieces of evidence against Keffe D came from Keffe D," trial attorney Shaun Kent told the BBC. "Keffe D has the right to take the stand and say 'I made all this up. I lied to sell copies of the book. I lied to the police. I'm a liar but I did not murder Tupac.'"

Davis has also publicly stated multiple times that Bad Boy Records head Sean "Diddy" Combs had offered him $1m to kill Death Row Records rivals Tupac and Knight.

News.title: Record 230 people cross Channel in one small boat
News.content:
A small boat has crossed the English Channel carrying 230 people, the largest number to make the journey in a single vessel.

It breaks the previous record set in July, when 165 people made the crossing on a single vessel.

The boat arrived in the UK in the early hours of Monday.

A picture taken off the coast of northern France showed the inflatable boat was so full many passengers had to dangle their legs in the water as it entered the busy shipping route.

A Home Office spokesperson said this latest incident demonstrated the "reckless and dangerous tactics employed by criminal gangs... who continue to put lives at risk by cramming ever greater numbers of people onto unseaworthy vessels".

French rescuers said the 15m (49ft) boat was "buckling" in the water and could have led to a "tragedy".

The boat was already carrying about 50 people when it was seen heading towards a beach to pick more passengers up, the crew in Berck-sur-Mer added.

French maritime officials said 30 migrants were left stranded by the tide during a boarding attempt at Berck beach in northern France.

They were brought to safety by maritime and land-based rescue services, the statement from France's Channel and North Sea Maritime Prefecture said.

The boat carrying 232 people continued its journey, before two passengers requested assistance and were taken to Calais by a French Navy rescue ship, the statement added.

News.title: New weight loss pill approved for use in UK
News.content:
A daily weight-loss pill made by the drug firm behind the Mounjaro jab has been approved for use in the UK - the first country in Europe to do so.

Foundayo, made by Eli Lilly, is for treating obesity and type 2 diabetes.

But while people will be able to buy it privately with a prescription, the approval by the Medicines and Healthcare productors Regulatory Agency does not automatically mean it will be made available on the NHS.

Foundayo is a form of GLP-1 medication that blunts appetite, and comes after the MHRA approved a pill version of a similar weight-loss drug, Wegovy, in June.

Eli Lilly said while it could immediately be used by the NHS for type 2 diabetes, it would be making an application to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence in England for it to be recommended as a weight loss treatment as well.

Dr Simon Cork, from Anglia Ruskin University, said while the weight-loss benefits of Foundayo were less than other treatments, patients could still expect to see "significant, clinically meaningful changes to their weight".

And he said a key advantage was that it was likely to be cheaper than other weight-loss treatments, which have tended to be tightly restricted by the NHS.

University of Glasgow expert Prof Naveed Sattar agreed it was "good news".

He said another benefit was its convenience, pointing out that unlike the Wegovy pill, which has to be taken on an empty stomach, this pill could be taken at any time of the day.

"The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences," he added.

Experts believe it could help people coming off weight-loss jabs remain slim.

Trials found that patients who had used weight loss jabs and then been given the tablet, also called orforglipron, every day for a year avoided regaining much of the weight they had lost - a known risk when coming off GLP-1 injections.

People on weight loss medication are also advised to eat a healthy diet and get enough exercise.

And, like any medication, there can be side effects to using Foundayo, including nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and vomiting.

News.title: Consortium including Jeff Bezos advances talks for stake in Liverpool FC
News.content:
A consortium including billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has advanced its talks to buy about a 30% stake in Liverpool, BBC Sport has been told.

The group is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

Owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed last month that the group had "expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club".

Bhatia is the son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal and had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.

American businessman Bezos, founder of e-commerce giant Amazon, is the fourth-richest person in the world.

According to Forbes, the 62-year-old has an estimated net worth of $256bn (Â£192bn).

FSG, who bought Liverpool in a Â£300m deal in 2010, previously sold a minority stake in the Anfield side to global sports investment firm Dynasty Equity.

BBC Sport contacted FSG about the latest developments, but they had no further comment.

In January, Liverpool became the top-earning Premier League club for the first time, according to analysis from financial firm Deloitte.

The following month the club announced record revenues of Â£703m for 2024-25 financial year.

News.title: MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
News.content:
A newly-elected MSP has apologised for the hurt caused by comments in which they talked of the "demonisation" of rape.

Scottish Green Party politician Q Manivannan has also faced criticism for suggesting rape is a "spectrum of things" during a podcast recorded before they were elected to the Scottish Parliament.

Earlier, the Scottish Rape Crisis Alliance (SRCA) - which represents four rape crisis centres - said there is "no hierarchy of rape" and warned the MSP not to minimise sexual violence.

In a statement, Manivannan said clips from the podcast had been "selectively edited" but said they were "sorry" for the upset, and insisted they would never seek to diminish a rape survivor's experience.

The comments, which were made during The Subjective Space podcast , externalrecorded last year, sparked fury after they re-emerged online at the weekend.

News.title: From Dubai to a Dublin court - how alleged cartel boss Daniel Kinahan returned to Ireland
News.content:
Armed police took up positions at the entrances to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin, as the plane carrying Daniel Kinahan approached the city.

On the steps of the building, journalists from Irish and international media tracked the flight online.

The Irish government had sent its jet to Dubai.

It is usually used to transport ministers, but it left the United Arab Emirates (UAE) with a suspected crime boss on board.

The doors of the court opened around half an hour after the aircraft landed at a military airfield nine miles (14km) away.

As reporters went through security, we heard the sound of sirens outside - indicating the arrival of the accused.

The courtroom filled up over the next 45 minutes - as detectives, prosecutors, and some members of the public took up seats along with the media.

From the moment Kinahan entered the dock, until he was led out 13 minutes later, almost everyone was looking towards him - and the proceedings were accompanied by constant typing from the press benches.

Complex international investigations, and diplomacy, had led to this moment.

Kinahan was charged with a single offence - directing the activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.

He did not have to enter a plea at this stage of the court process.

But his lawyers have previously told the BBC that the allegations he is a crime boss are false and have no evidential basis.

They also said he had no criminal record or convictions.

News.title: From Stonehenge to the Serpentine - satellite images show impact of hot, dry summer
News.content:
With more parts of England set to join Wales as being officially declared to be in drought, BBC Verify has been gathering satellite imagery showing the impact of this year's extreme summer heat.

From historic sites and parks to reservoirs and golf courses, the hot, dry weather has changed how large parts of the UK usually look.

This year's consecutive heatwaves and above-average temperatures have had a noticeable effect - even compared with last summer which was the UK's warmest on record.

News.title: Six arrested after woman found dead in north London
News.content:
Six people have been arrested on suspicion of murder following the death of a 23-year-old woman in north London.

Police were called at 09:33 BST on Thursday, following concerns for the welfare of a woman at a residential address on Bollinder Place, Clerkenwell.

Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and found an unresponsive woman, who was pronounced dead at the scene.

Four women, aged 20, 21, 23, and 26, and two men, aged 21 and 24 were arrested at the scene. All six have since been released on bail while enquiries continue.

Work is ongoing to trace the woman's next-of-kin, who will be supported by specially trained officers once identified.

Ch Supt Jason Stewart said: "This is a tragic incident and our thoughts remain with the family and friends of the young woman who has lost her life.

"We understand that news of an incident like this will cause concern within the local community."

News.title: Nigel Farage says incident at his home 'directly linked' to Ann Widdecombe murder
News.content:
Nigel Farage said an incident at his London home last year was "directly linked" to the murder of Ann Widdecombe, after counter-terror police reopened an inquiry into it last week.

It relates to what Farage described as a "lit incendiary device" being pushed through his letterbox in April 2025, the BBC understands.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London has also referred itself to the police watchdog over how the initial investigation was handled.

At a Monday press conference, the Reform UK leader said: "I understand this is a completely unprecedented move, and yes, this is directly linked to the murder of Ann Widdecombe, and I'm afraid I just can't tell you any more than that at this stage."

News.title: Hope of finding mum's body 'lost if killer released'
News.content:
The court heard evidence from a domestic abuse report Linda made to police before her death, which showed she feared he would kill her.

Linda said that when she confronted Razzell about an affair he had with a 19-year-old in 2000, he threw her so hard she cracked a rib. He also made threats to kill her, she had told officers.

Razzell was tried and acquitted of two counts of domestic abuse a few months before he killed Linda.

However, a Parole Board hearing in 2023 concluded on the balance of probabilities that he was abusive.

In a victim statement played in court, Linda's cousin Westmore said a "huge chunk of happiness and joy" had been taken from her family's lives.

Linda's mother had died when she was eight and she went to live with Judy, meaning the pair grew up like sisters.

Westmore continued: "The major impact on myself and our family would be a loss of trust in the justice system of this country if he [Razzell] is released without saying where Linda's remains are.

"It's chilling that Glyn Razzell can calmly present as an innocent trustworthy man.

"If Glyn is released, all hope of ever finding Linda's remains will be lost."

Razzell, who wore a black suit in court, has applied for parole four times. When his application was refused in 2021, he became the first prisoner to be denied parole under Helen's Law.

The law requires the Parole Board to take into consideration a killer's refusal to disclose where they hid their victim's body.

The court also heard that he contributes to a website, easily found online, which claims he is innocent.

News.title: Asylum seeker who groomed and raped girl, 13, jailed
News.content:
An asylum seeker who raped a 13-year-old girl after pretending to be a teenager on Snapchat has been jailed.

Abdul Khan attacked the girl in a nature reserve in Clifton, Nottingham, on 14 May last year.

Khan arrived in the UK in the back of a lorry in 2015, Nottingham Crown Court heard, and faces automatic deportation to Afghanistan after he has served two thirds of his sentence.

He was jailed for nine and a half years on Monday after he was convicted of two counts of rape, one count of sexual activity with a child, sexual communication with a child, meeting a child following grooming and perverting the course of justice.

A four-day trial was told Khan, who is believed to be 28 and already serving a 23-month sentence for sexual communication with a different child in Derbyshire, arranged to meet his victim in woodland after telling her on the Snapchat messaging app he was a 14-year-old boy.

When they met in person and it was clear he was not 14, he tried to appease her by claiming to be 16, the court heard.

After activity that jurors found had been consensual, Khan, of HMP Nottingham, twice raped the girl.

Judge Mark Watson said the victim told her father what had happened and he contacted police.

Khan was then linked to the rapes by a mobile phone seized during his arrest over his contact with the child in Derbyshire.

Yet despite DNA evidence subsequently linking him to the attack, Nottinghamshire Police said he continued to deny having met the victim.

Addressing Khan, the judge said: "You deliberately concealed your true identity. She thought she was communicating with a child of her own age.

"It was a lie you have persisted with throughout these proceedings."

News.title: Two more Thetford disorder arrests takes total to 15
News.content:
Two more arrests have been made following three nights of unrest in a Norfolk town.

Disorder linked to anti-immigration protests took place in Thetford in Norfolk on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, with a police presence in the area ever since.

Norfolk Police said a man in his 20s, arrested on Sunday on suspicion of assaulting an emergency worker and being in possession of a Class B drug, remains in custody.

A teenage boy, arrested on suspicion of assaulting an emergency worker, was taken to Bury St Edmunds Police Investigation Centre and has since been released on bail until 4 October.

The force has made 15 arrests in total since the disorder started last week.

News.title: British couple held in Iran end hunger strike
News.content:
A British couple jailed in Iran after being accused of espionage have ended their hunger strikes after 93 and 84 days respectively.

Craig and Lindsay Foreman were arrested in January 2025 while passing through Iran on a motorcycle journey from Europe to Australia. They were both sentenced to 10 years in jail in February, but Craig Foreman's family said his punishment had been extended by two years after speaking to the media.

The couple from East Sussex, who both deny espionage, went on hunger strike in May when prison authorities prevented them from calling their families.

The family of the couple said they had been protesting against how they and other prisoners were being treated.

A spokesperson for the family said the couple agreed with prison guards to end their strike to be able to speak directly to their loved ones again.

However, the family said contact was yet to be re-established, as of Monday afternoon.

The family had also previously called for the couple to end their hunger strike.

Five people outside the prison joined the pair on their hunger strike for the final five days from Tuesday to Saturday as an act of solidarity, the family added.

Lindsay Foreman's son Joe Bennett and four unnamed others took part in the UK, as well as other prisoners inside Tehran's Evin jail, the family said.

"My mum and Craig have spent months on hunger strike, and even at the point of bringing it to an end they wanted to make it about something bigger than themselves," Bennett, from Folkestone in Kent, said.

"Those final five days became about people standing together around values that should be universal: Truth, justice, kindness, peace and unity."

By the end of the protest, Craig Foreman had been on hunger strike for 93 days, and Lindsay Foreman for 84 days, the family added.

Although they said they were unaware of the condition of the pair, who had consumed just milk and either honey or salt in water during their strikes.

Bennett said the couple also went on a separate hunger striker back in November as a "cry out for help".

News.title: Owner of 250-year-old Grade II-listed windmill gave it colourful makeover without permission
News.content:
Dr Eiddwen Jones, 85, is the great-great-great-great-great-granddaughter of Thomas Jones, who she said was the first miller at Llynon mill in 1776.

He managed the property in the village of Llanddeusant, Anglesey, until he died in his nineties.

She said the windmill should be repainted in whitewash as it is a historical building, and traditionally "that's how the mills were".

The author, whose family moved from Anglesey to Flintshire 150 years ago, said she did not agree that the windmill was painted in the first place to celebrate the Eisteddfod.

She has visited the windmill several times throughout her life where Thomas Jones' name is painted inside, and said he "would have turned in his grave, I believe," if he had known about its new appearance.

Jones added that it looked "very impressive in its original colour" when driving towards it.

"It's been made fun of now rather than kept the fact that it was a historical building and that people have been working there for a couple of centuries," she said.

Holt said the mill can be hard to find for visitors, as it is not close to the A55 road.

But the new colours have sparked a lot of interest.

With winters especially proving difficult with fewer people coming, he added: "I have a duty to ensure the future of the mill for the next generation."

He apologised to the local authority, saying he "realises that they [the council] are only doing their job and I know that I have broken the rules".

But he added: "I'm struggling and the winter is hard, but painting the mill has attracted more visitors here and helped me pay the bills."

He is gathering the opinions of visitors to the mill this summer to make a case to the council.

News.title: Suffolk heathland fire stood down as major incident
News.content:
A heathland fire which engulfed an area the size of 210 football pitches in Suffolk has been stood down as a major incident, almost two weeks after the blaze broke out.

Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said the decision followed a fire risk assessment of Dunwich Heath and RSPB Minsmere.

The service stressed "the incident itself is not over" and said people must stay away from the heathland, where firefighters remained to dampen down, monitor for hotspots, and any further fire activity.

Jon Lacey, the county's chief fire officer, said the decision to stand down the major incident reflected the "significant progress made by our crews and everyone who has supported this response".

President Donald Trump is set to sign an executive order that would significantly alter the federal guidance for childhood vaccines and call for states to reconsider their guidance for vaccine requirements for school, upending decades of public health practice in a move aimed at pleasing the conspiracy theorists and anti-vaccine activists who embraced his political movement in the years following the Covid-19 pandemic.

Speaking in the Oval Office on Monday, the president called the move an “ historic step in our mission to make America healthy again” before going on to regurgitate long-discredited theories about the non-existent link between vaccines and autism.

“My administration is recognizing gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases,” said Trump, who added that the Measles, Mumps and Rubella vaccine that has been used since 1971 would once again be broken up into three separate vaccines despite the lack of any such separate vaccines on the current market.

Citing no evidence, he alleged that the MMR vaccine — long a boogeyman of anti-vaccine activists thanks to a long-discredited study by a disgraced British ex-physician.

“So the MMR, we want to have separate, separate visits, separate times. The vaccine being broken into three separate single doses, and vaccines being administered in separate visits,” he said.

Trump also announced that vaccines for Covid-19, Influenza and Hepatitis B would no longer be recommended, despite warning from health experts that not vaccinating against the liver disease could give rise to an epidemic of liver cancer years down the road in unvaccinated children infected with the virus.

“Parents can still choose to give their children all of the vaccinations if they wish. It's up to the parents. We're making recommendations that are strong, but it's up to the parents if they wish, and they will be covered by insurance,” he said.

“Decades ago, children received only a small fraction of the vaccines required today. In those times, people were much healthier, and of course, the high rates of autism now observed did not exist. So, it is a reason for such epidemic rates of autism, and we're going to bring it back to much closer to where it was.”

There is no evidence linking vaccination rates to autism, yet Trump and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long pushed the theory that vaccines–particularly the meales, mumps and rubella vaccine–is liked to autism spectrum disorder.

This comes despite the fact that multiple studies have debunked the supposed link between childhood vaccinations and children developing autism spectrum disorder. Andrew Wakefield, the physician who published the original study, later had his medical license revoked and The Lancet retracted the study.

The executive order, entitled “Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations,” would divide childhood vaccinations into three distinct categories: immunizations recommended for all children such as the MMR vaccine, diptheria, tetanus and polio; vaccines for high-risk groups or populations like hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccines; and vaccines based on shared clinical decisionmaking such as the Covid-19 vaccine and the flu shot.

In addition, the executive order recommends that the MMR vaccine be broken up into three separate single shots. The order also advises states to review the recommendations and “consider updating relevant laws and regulations that define” immunization requirements.

Trump has for years, going back to his 2016 run for president, suggested that vaccines should be administered in smaller doses.

News.content:

Fans are rallying around Matthew Lillard after a bitter former fan confronted him at a horror convention.

The Scream actor, 56, was answering questions from fans at the Midsummer Scream event in Long Beach, California, over the weekend when a man came to the microphone and started an awkward dialogue with the movie star.

Video from the event shared on social media showed the man telling Lillard, who helped him hold up the microphone, “I met you a few years ago.”

The man proceeded to tell Lillard that when they previously met, he tried to tell him his theory about a connection between the hit 1996 slasher movie and the 1995 romance Mad Love — which Lillard appeared in — due to both films featuring Drew Barrymore as characters named Casey.

He said that in response to his idea, Lillard responded at the time by saying, “What were you smoking?”

open image in gallery Matthew Lillard was confronted by a bitter former fan at a recent horror convention ( Getty )

“The way you made me feel...when you told me that, you kind of lost me as a fan,” the person told Lillard. “I just wanted you to know that.”

Lillard paused for a moment before quipping, “Okay. What a great question.”

The crowd’s reaction to the interaction began to drown out the man’s voice, but he continued to speak to Lillard before concluding, “I always had a thing for you, so I just wanted you to know you lost me as a fan. Thank you.”

Fans in the audience then erupted into booing the man as he finished speaking.

However, Lillard appeared unfazed by the awkward moment and walked away from the man to a different section of the crowd. When actor Jamie Kennedy then asked Lillard what had happened, he responded, “It does not matter.”

open image in gallery Lillard said that t ( Getty )

After people attending the convention were quick to hop to Lillard’s defense by booing the critic, his online fanbase posted messages of support for the Scooby-Doo star.

“Why would you even wait to bring that up? How petty are you sir to make him feel bad? Matthew is soooo sweet and caring,” one person wrote on Instagram. Another added: “Protect Matthew Lillard at all costs.”

“Who goes to an event to hate on somebody?!!” a third wondered in the Instagram comments.

Another wrote on X, “When the f*** did people decide it was okay to publicly gang up on Matthew Lillard, literally one of the sweetest guys in show business?”

The Independent has contacted Lillard’s representatives for comment.

Parents are being warned that fake or counterfeit versions of their children’s favorite toys may put them in danger.

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission warned in an August 5 notice against fake or counterfeit squishy toys — and cautioned against a viral social media trend that encourages children and teens to microwave them.

These toys, which can resemble popular characters, animals or food, are sold online, on social media and at discount stores and other retailers.

Viral videos show these toys expanding, changing texture or even bursting when they are heated up.

However, the commission warns that these trends are “dangerous and should never be attempted or imitated.”

In January, a 9-year-old boy in Plainfield, Illinois, suffered burns to his face and hands when he microwaved a NeeDoh toy, which exploded, covering him in scalding goo, reported the New York Times. The youngster was taken to the emergency room and later transferred to a burn center where he was treated for second-degree burns .

open image in gallery Counterfeit versions of trendy squishy toys may put kids in danger, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission warned ( The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission )

Some versions of them do not comply with federal safety requirements for children’s toys. Some squishy toys contain water beads, gels, liquids, powders or sand. If the toys burst, children may be exposed to the contents.

“Water beads can expand after being swallowed and cause intestinal blockages, choking, aspiration, or injuries when inserted into the nose or ear. Other unknown filling materials may present chemical exposure, inhalation, or ingestion hazards,” the CPSC warned.

The CPSC also warned that some fake toys may break or tear during use, releasing hazardous materials or contain excessive amounts of lead, prohibited phthalates or other chemicals.

Some also fail to comply with federal requirements governing water beads, lack required warnings, age grading, tracking information or manufacturer identification. They may also be sold without testing and certification required for children’s products.

The commission has identified 55 shipments of these dangerous toys at U.S. ports, and worked with U.S. Customs and Border Protection to prevent 355,683 units from entering the country.

open image in gallery The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission warned that these toys may break or tear, releasing hazardous materials that may harm children ( The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission )

The CPSC recommends that parents and caregivers purchase toys from reputable retailers, be cautious of unusually low prices, check packaging for misspelled words or missing manufacturer information or safety warnings and keep damaged toys away from children.

The commission says that if a burn should occur as a result of the toys, the affected area should immediately be placed under cool running water for at least 20 minutes.

Gently washing the area with mild soap and water also helps to remove any remaining material.

Medical attention should be sought for a severe burn, a burn involving a young child, or if there are signs of an infection after the burn.

U.S. health officials have proposed a rule change that would require food producers to inform authorities prior to introducing new ingredients or additives into packaged and processed goods.

This measure seeks to alter a long-standing policy criticized by advocates as a regulatory loophole that has permitted thousands of unvetted substances to enter the nation's food supply.

Under the Food and Drug Administration's draft regulation, businesses would be required to document and present written safety justifications for new ingredients, allowing officials to examine potential hazards. Currently, manufacturers independently determine whether an ingredient qualifies as "generally recognized as safe," or GRAS, without any obligation to report or submit evidence to the agency, though a subset of companies does so voluntarily.

"Shifting to a mandatory notification system closes a decades-old information gap, giving the FDA the comprehensive visibility needed to enhance postmarket safety," acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas told reporters on Monday.

open image in gallery RFK Jr. delivers remarks during an event at HHS Headquarters Monday that highlighted a series of 'landmark actions' to improve the nation's food supply and advance the 'Make America Healthy Again' agenda ( Getty Images )

A 120-day public comment window has been opened by the agency to gather feedback on the plan.

Susan Mayne, former director of FDA's food program, observed that while the rule would provide the agency with improved oversight of the wide array of market additives, only a minor fraction would face formal evaluation.

"This is a reasonable first step towards a more complete inventory, but most self-affirmed GRAS ingredients will still not be reviewed for safety by the FDA, with food ingredient safety continuing to be risk-based," said Mayne, who is now a public health expert at Yale University.

Additionally, the FDA intends to make public a directory of submissions provided by manufacturers. Mayne emphasized that consumers must recognize that "inclusion on the list would not mean FDA thinks the ingredient is safe."

Scrutiny of ultraprocessed food continues, but with few details

In a related step, the agency announced it has finalized the federal government's initial formal definition for ultraprocessed foods, though specific wording and details remain undisclosed. The draft definition has been forwarded to the White House for further evaluation.

Public health proponents view a standardized definition as a critical milestone toward examining products linked to widespread chronic illnesses in the population. A formal baseline could facilitate expanded federal research and lay the groundwork for potential future restrictions or mandatory warning labels.

Neither measure is anticipated to instantly alter consumer eating habits, which remain heavy in sugar, sodium, and fats that contribute to conditions including heart disease, diabetes, and obesity. Nevertheless, these efforts align with the central agenda of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who assumed office with a pledge to target synthetic dyes, additives, and related compounds.

"These two actions will change how the federal government oversees what’s in our food and how we understand the foods that Americans eat," Kennedy said at an event Monday at HHS headquarters.

Ultraprocessed items undergo industrial manufacturing processes involving additives, colorings, preservatives, and other elements absent from home cooking. Common examples comprise soft drinks, sweetened breakfast cereals, snack chips, frozen pizzas, and processed grocery goods.

Researchers have spent more than ten years trying to establish standardized classifications for processed foods. However, broad criteria present challenges, as they may capture items such as whole wheat bread, granola, and yogurt—foods that undergo substantial processing yet maintain nutritional value. Recent classification frameworks have incorporated specific exemptions for items fulfilling established dietary standards regardless of their processing level.

FDA proposal would bring new insights on additives used by food companies

Approximately 10,000 chemical additives, including thickeners, preservatives, and packaging substances, are currently permitted across the domestic food supply.

Advocacy groups have maintained for years that many of these compounds lack rigorous safety evaluations due to the FDA practice allowing companies to self-certify additives under the "generally recognized as safe," or GRAS, designation.

Diamantas clarified on Monday that the proposed adjustments would not force every new ingredient to undergo a full agency evaluation, noting that mandatory pre-market approvals would require legislative action from Congress.

"What we’re doing is requiring companies that utilize the pathway to notify us of their conclusions so that we have greater visibility," Diamantas said.

open image in gallery In a related step, the FDA announced it has finalized the federal government's initial formal definition for ultraprocessed foods, though specific wording and details remain undisclosed ( AP Photo/Manuel Balce Ceneta )

Framework guidelines specify a 180-day window for the agency to review filings. Should health officials identify potential safety issues, they could seek supplementary data or request that the manufacturer postpone launching the ingredient.

Reform advocates argue that mere notification does not go far enough.

"It must also include strong, science-based safety standards and thorough, independent FDA review before chemicals are allowed in our food," said Melanie Benesh of the nonprofit Environmental Working Group.

Kennedy indicated that the Trump administration intends to petition Congress to grant the FDA expanded authority over food additives.

"Congress needs to give FDA the additional tools it needs to keep pace with the changing food supply and protect the American people," Kennedy said.

A rule change in the 1990s created what advocates call a loophole

In principle, any intentional food additive requires formal agency authorization unless deemed inherently safe. Since the late 1950s, federal oversight has acknowledged that staple items like vinegar and spices are widely consumed and traditionally regarded as harmless.

Although the agency originally evaluated GRAS exemptions directly, the process proved resource-intensive. Beginning in 1997, the FDA authorized food producers to independently decide whether a new substance was safe based on published research and expert consensus.

Over time, the inventory of self-certified GRAS substances expanded to encompass numerous natural and synthetic additives, which entered commercial distribution without external government evaluation.

Health advocacy organizations, including the Center for Science in the Public Interest, contend this framework created a "secret GRAS loophole."

Industry representatives maintain that corporate safety evaluations are every bit as comprehensive as formal regulatory reviews.

News.title: Powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake hits Colombia leaving at least 111 dead and more trapped
News.content:

At least 111 people have been killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, tearing down buildings across several cities and leaving others trapped in the rubble.

Colombia's president Abelardo De La Espriella said at least 87 people were injured and declared an emergency to expedite funding for the recovery while saying he would visit the disaster zone.

The 7.4 magnitude quake struck near San José del Palmar, some 150 miles west of Bogotá, at 7.34am local time on Monday, with tremors felt in major cities nationwide.

The highest reported death toll was in the western province of Risaralda in Colombia's coffee-growing region, where authorities reported 42 fatalities.

Britain’s foreign office advised against all but essential travel to parts of Colombia, reporting the closure of six airports and warning of the possibility of aftershocks.

Have you been affected? Contact james.reynolds@independent.co.uk

The quake struck just days after far-right populist Mr De La Espriella was sworn in as president, thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis.

open image in gallery Residents dig through the debris of a collapsed building after an earthquake, in Cali on Monday ( Reuters )

"We aren't going to leave people alone. They are in our hearts and we are going to tend to people with our full determination," the president said.

At least 18 people were killed in Pereira, mayor Mauricio Salazar told Caracol Radio, while others continue to remain trapped in collapsed buildings.

Two others were killed in Manizales, mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas said in an interview with Blu Radio. The number of people injured is yet to be confirmed.

One person died in Buenaventura, Colombia's main Pacific port, when a building collapsed, trapping several people, authorities said.

And people remained trapped in Cali, one of Colombia's largest cities, after more than two dozen structures collapsed, mayor Alejandro Eder said.

open image in gallery People look for survivors amid the rubble of a collapsed building after an earthquake in Cali, Colombia ( AFP/Getty )

He added that the city had asked authorities in Bogota and Medellin to send disaster teams to support rescue efforts.

“At this point, two people have already been rescued alive, one elderly woman and one young girl. There are more people trapped,” Eder told Blu Radio.

“We have at least 12 critical points and 25 collapsed structures that we are responding to.”

De La Espriella said in a video filmed while flying to Bogota that he was suspending his planned activities to lead emergency coordination efforts out of the capital.

open image in gallery The Manizales Cathedral was among the buildings damaged by the tremors ( AFP/Getty )

Colombia's civil aviation authority said flights were suspended at airports in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura while inspectors checked for structural damage.

Initial statements suggested that the quake’s depth was 79km before this was upgraded to 96km (60 miles) with the tremor magnitude increased to 7.4.

Witnesses in the Venezuelan border state of Tachira and the central-western city of Barquisimeto reported the quake had been felt there.

No tsunami warning was issued in the aftermath of the incident, the US tsunami warning system confirmed.

Reports from nine departments and all 32 departmental capitals where the quake was experienced were received by Colombia’s disaster agency triggering evacuations and damage reports.

The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management in Colombia said it is in communication with local officials to evaluate potential damage but no major destruction has been reported in the capital.

open image in gallery People look for survivors amid the rubble of a collapsed building after the earthquake hit Cali ( AFP/Getty )

The region was hit by devastating twin earthquakes near Caracas in Venezuela in June, which killed over 6,000 people. Witnesses told Reuters that they felt the tremors in the border state of Tachira and the central-western city of Barquisimeto.

Colombia’s location on the Pacific Ring of Fire makes it highly susceptible to earthquakes. The Ring of Fire is a belt where the Earth’s tectonic plates meet, with around 90 per cent of the planet’s largest earthquakes occurring here.

The country’s most devastating quake occurred in August 1868, killing around 70,000 people.
