Conservative podcaster Tucker Carlson claimed Monday that Israeli figures falsely told him Hunter Biden’s laptop contained graphic images of children.

Carlson, who once used the laptop story to criticize the Biden family while serving as a Fox News anchor, put to rest conspiracy theories about the laptop’s contents in a wide-ranging interview with the former president’s son – specifically the false allegations that the laptop contained abusive images of children.

“Can I just say one thing though, this is what I experienced during that time - the allegation that there was abusive minors proven on the laptop – that came from the Israelis,” Carlson told Biden.

While Biden’s laptop contained nude images of himself and women, there were no explicit images or videos of children. Allegations of such were the result of online conspiracy theories.

The “Tucker Carlson Show” host went further and claimed a man “connected to [Isreali Prime Minister] Netanyahu” had given a producer on his former Fox News show the misinformation about Biden’s laptop directly.

open image in gallery Tucker Carlson accused Israelis of spreading misinformation about the contents on Hunter Biden’s laptop ( The Tucker Carlson Show )

“They were behind that,” Carlson insisted.

The Independent has asked the Isreali government for comment.

Carlson did not provide further details about the alleged exchange with an Isreali connected to Netanyahu.

The Hunter Biden laptop controversy unfolded in 2020 after the New York Post published an article alleging emails from the laptop’s hard drive proved corruption among the Biden family. Trump’s former lawyer, Rudy Giuliani, reportedly provided the information to the news outlet.

The story became political drama because some social media platforms blocked access to the article, out of concern that it was Russian disinformation. Conservatives accused social media companies and liberal groups of censorship.

Among those who frequently discussed the laptop story was Carlson, who spent more than 2 hours of airtime on the topic within weeks of the New York Post article coming out, according to an estimate by Media Matters for America.

open image in gallery Carlson, who once campaigned for Trump, has recently broken from the MAGA movement and sought to unify disgruntled conservatives ( AFP/Getty )

Six years later, Carlson sat across from Biden, giving the former president’s son the space to deny accusations associated with the laptop controversy – including those of corruption between himself and his father before the 2020 presidential election.

This is a breaking news story, more follows...

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.content:

The Blues are one of 11 Premier League teams vying to win the first piece of silverware up for grabs next season.

Sports.title: Arsenal misfit Gabriel Jesus lined up for Italian job with Napoli as transfer replacement for Romelu Lukaku
Sports.content:
ARSENAL striker Gabriel Jesus has emerged as a target for Napoli.

The Italian club wants to bring in the Brazilian as a replacement for Romelu Lukaku, who they are trying to sell.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United striker is attracting interest from Fenerbahce and is open to moving to Turkey.



Arsenal are ready to cash in on Jesus, 29, as he is into the final 12 months of his contract at the Emirates.



The striker made just 14 Premier League appearances last season and scored three goals after battling back from a serious knee injury.

Napoli could offer the Brazilian more game time, but his wages may prove to be a stumbling block.

Jesus is thought to be on over £200,000-a-week at the Emirates after joining from Manchester City for £45million four years ago.

He has slipped down the pecking order since then and Mikel Arteta can now call upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres to lead the line.

Arsenal are hoping to sell players before this summer’s transfer window shuts.

Reiss Nelson, who has one year left on his contract, is a target for West Ham.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Hamburg had Fabio Vieira on loan last season and want to make his stay permanent.



Gabriel Martinelli would be a high-profile departure – but it is not yet certain that Arsenal will sell him.

The Brazilian is into the final 12 months of his contract, however there is the option to extend it by a further year.

Galatasaray have been linked with a move for the winger and they are one of those tracking AC Milan star Rafael Leao.

Arsenal, however, are unlikely to sanction the sale of Martinelli unless they can sign a new left winger.

The Gunners were interested in Vinicius Junior, but he signed a new deal with Real Madrid last week.

Sports.title: BBC to show new football league on free-to-air TV in major broadcasting change
Sports.content:
THE BBC has struck a major new deal to show live football free-to-air for the next three seasons.

BBC Cymru Wales has agreed a three-year broadcasting partnership with the Football Association of Wales to screen matches from the Novira Cymru Premier.



The agreement will see a minimum of 20 games per season broadcast live on BBC iPlayer, with the deal running until 2029.

Fans will also be able to follow extensive coverage and updates from Wales’ top flight through BBC Sport Online.



The first game shown under the agreement will be Barry Town United against Cardiff Met on Saturday, August 15, with kick-off at 12.30pm.

Both sides have won their opening two matches of the campaign, while Ammanford versus Connah’s Quay Nomads will then be shown on August 22.

BBC Wales head of sport Carolyn Hitt said: “This deal strengthens our commitment to provide live coverage of Welsh football, and follows our recent announcement to show all of the Uefa Wales men’s international games up until Euro 2028.”

She added: “We hope this will be welcome news to Welsh football fans as we continue to bring sport to free-to-air television.”

The deal comes amid a major revamp of the Cymru Premier, which has expanded from 12 to 16 clubs for its 35th edition, with matches predominantly switching to Friday evenings.

Llandudno, Airbus UK, Holywell Town, Trefelin BGC, Cambrian United and Ammanford have all been promoted into the expanded division.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

FAW head of domestic leagues Jack Sharp said: “This agreement represents another significant step in growing the profile of the Novira Cymru Premier, enabling us to reach more supporters across Wales and the wider UK through increased free-to-air coverage.”

He added: “The BBC’s commitment to Welsh domestic football will play an important role in increasing awareness of the league, attracting new audiences, and supporting our wider ambition to continue growing the game.”

Sports.title: Turkish journalist DETAINED by police ‘for saying Jamal Musiala was going to sign for Galatasaray’
Sports.content:
TURKISH journalist Burhan Can Terzi was shockingly detained by police after reporting Galatasaray were close to signing Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala.

According to Haberler, Terzi was held by order of the Bakırkoy chief public prosecutor’s office on charges of “publicly disseminating misleading information”.



This is the first high-profile detention of a sports journalist under these allegations in Turkey.

Gazzetta added that the reporter was let go just a few hours later without any restrictions imposed on him.



Terzi reported on July 26 that Galata had “largely agreed” with Musiala, 23, but the club issued a stern statement denying that claim.

Galatasaray‘s announcement read: “Recently, the need to inform the public about our club has been deliberately circulated and does not reflect the truth.

“The allegations that professional football player Jamal Musiala will transfer to Galatasaray are untrue.

“Keeping these allegations, which are clearly unreal, on the agenda; it is an effort to create a perception aimed at misleading the public and discrediting the transfer efforts of our club.

“It is noteworthy that the people and media who own these speculations came to the public with similar unreal claims last season.

“Galatasaray carry out transfer activities with great meticulousness and confidentiality in line with the interests of our club.



“Unreal news and speculative claims will not change the working principles and goals of our club.

“We kindly request that the public and the great Galatasaray fans take only the official statements of our club as a basis, not to respect the news and speculations that do not reflect the truth, the people and media that persistently put them into circulation.”

According to NTV, Terzi stood by his information insisting his findings regarding Musiala and Galatasaray were based on truth.

The journalist responded: “Simultaneously, Musiala would attend the camp next week from different sources.

“I’m not in the mood to get up in the morning to make it up or see it in my dreams at night.”



Terzi’s career started after graduating from Istanbul University where he studied Journalism.

He started out at Fotospor in 2009 and then worked as an editor as well as assistant director of sports at Guneş before moving to Aksam.

The Turkish journo quickly crossed over to TV as he took part in football programs on TGRT and BenguTurk.

He is also among the founding partners of Sportcell Media and has ben covering Galatasaray for years.

According to Halk TV, Terzi clashed with the Turkish giants last year when he claimed club president Dursun Ozbek would have lost the 2022 elections to Esref Hamamcioglu if it wasn’t for controversial former director Erden Timur.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Timur was arrested in December as part of a major investigation into betting and match-fixing in Turkish football.

The former Galatasaray chief was jailed for about six months as part of a pre-trial detention and released in June under judicial supervision while the investigation continues.

Sports.title: Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh PULLS OUT of deal to take over Championship giants after months of talks
Sports.content:
SAUDI boxing chief Turki Alalshikh has pulled the plug on his takeover of Derby County.

The Championship club had the purchase sanctioned by the Independent Football Regulator and the EFL last week.



But Alalshikh, who owns Lion Sport, is no longer going ahead with the deal and the Rams are off the market.

A statement from Derby read: “The club can confirm discussions with Lion Sport to buy a controlling interest in Derby County will no longer proceed.



“The purchase process had been sanctioned by both the Independent Football Regulator and the EFL, notification of which the club received last week.

“However, today the club received notice that Lion Sport no longer wanted to continue with the purchase.



“For the benefit of any doubt, the club is now off the market and will continue to operate under the loyal, committed and unwavering support of Clowes Developments.

“Our preparations continue for the new EFL season, beginning against Charlton Athletic on Saturday.

“The club will offer no further comment.”

Alalshikh has made his name in sport thanks to Saudi Arabia pushing to host the biggest fights in boxing.



The latest bout he is involved in is Anthony Joshua’s showdown with Tyson Fury, which is scheduled for later this year.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Alalshikh added: “After careful consideration, we don’t feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place.

“But we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future. I personally wish the team and club every success for the season ahead.”

Sports.title: Man Utd physio and Class of 92 star’s brother puts incredible shirt collection up for sale including David Beckham’s kit
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans have been the chance to get their hands on some Class of ’92 history.

A slew of iconic shirts worn by arguably the most popular players in the modern era have been put up for auction.



A collection of tops worn by David Beckham, Ryan Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville and Nicky Butt will be available for auction on MatchWornShirt.

Former Red Devils physio Rod Thornley has gifted FIVE shirts to the auction platform.



They include signed 2001/02 match-issued tops for Butt and Scholes.

Match issued 02/03 away tops for Beckham and Neville are also up for sale.



But the shirt most likely to fetch the highest fee is a 03/04 away top worn by Giggs in a Champions League clash with Olympiacos.

The Class of ’92 set went up for auction on August 4 and will be available to bid on until 4pm this Wednesday.

Thornley had much more than a working relationship with the Class of ’92.

His brother, Ben, was part of the academy set up and went on to make a total of 14 appearances for the Red Devils.



Reflecting on arguably Sir Alex Ferguson‘s best crop of players, Rod said: “I think it’s gotta be up there, one of the best youth teams ever for what they produced, definitely.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“The amount of players that came through that system all at the same time.

“I mean, there’s nothing like it since.”



Many of the Class of ’92 are still held in incredibly high regard, particularly Scholes.

Rod is among the many who believe the former England star would walk straight into Michael Carrick‘s starting XI.

He said: “I’d have to say Scholesy, I just loved him. He was brilliant.

“Even the superstars, Zidane, Xavi alike said that he was the best they ever played against.

“They know what they’re talking about.”

Sports.title: Newcastle fans fume ‘this is a new low’ as they are brutally rejected by No1 transfer target
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE fans have been left fuming after top transfer target Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg REJECTED a move to St James’ Park.

The Magpies had made the Marseille midfielder a priority as they desperately look to rebuild following a turbulent summer on Tyneside.



But transfer guru Fabrizio Romano reports that Hojbjerg’s proposed switch is now OFF following fresh talks.

Newcastle were reportedly prepared to meet Marseille’s demands for the 31-year-old former Tottenham star, only for the Denmark international to turn down their proposal.



And the rejection proved the final straw for some Toon supporters following a summer in which several of their biggest names have headed for the exit.

One fan raged: “I was never convinced with his signing but him actually turning us down is a new low #NUFC.”



Another supporter wrote: “Getting rejected by Hojbjerg is a new low. I’m just gutted I can’t bet on him to get a yellow card every week.”

While a third added: “Last thing we want is to have a player like him on an expensive long-term deal. He’s not worth it.”

The latest setback comes after Newcastle already lost Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali to Tottenham, with the latter’s departure bringing in the second-highest transfer fee in the club’s history.

Captain Bruno Guimaraes has since also departed for Arsenal, leaving a sizeable hole in the middle of the park which Newcastle had hoped Hojbjerg could help fill.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And the upheaval has not been confined to the playing squad, with Eddie Howe stepping down after almost five years in charge and former Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle replacing him.

There have been arrivals too, with the likes of goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, winger Bazoumana Toure and midfielder Sean Steur, but Hojbjerg’s snub represents another frustrating blow as Newcastle attempt to reshape their squad.

Jaissle now faces a race to strengthen his options before the transfer window closes, with Newcastle’s Premier League campaign beginning at home to Liverpool on Sunday August 23.

Sports.title: England stars’ World Cup bomb scare revealed after police dog ‘smelled EXPLOSIVES on team bus ahead of Argentina match
Sports.content:
ENGLAND’S stars were allegedly caught up in a World Cup bomb scare ahead of their semi-final clash against Argentina.

A leaked security services’ report, seen by Informacion.es, details a number of terror attempts including the targeting of the Three Lions’ team bus.



The horror unfolded before Harry Kane and co suffered a heartbreaking 2-1 defeat to Argentina in Atlanta on July 15, the Spanish outlet said.

The shocking documents revealed a police dog handler had marked an area of the England team bus as positive for explosives following claims there was a bomb onboard.



But the bomb scare was later confirmed to be a false alarm and was caused by a mechanical failure involving an oil leak.

They said of the threats posed at the World Cup: “The most concerning occurred when someone claimed there was a bomb on the bus transporting the England team to play the semi-final against Argentina.



“A canine agent (K-9) marked an area of the bus as positive for explosives. Another four-legged agent later corrected it. It was a false alarm caused by a mechanical failure involving an oil leak, according to the reports.”

The Sun has contacted The FA for comment.



The docs also revealed that an X user had threatened to attack the home of FIFA president Gianni Infantino if the controversial hydration breaks continued to be taken during World Cup matches.

The FBI is understood to have been made aware of the threat, although it wasn’t clear what action officials had taken to counter it.

US President Donald Trump was also reportedly the focus of several threats, according to Informacion.

One occurred on June 22 when an individual published an AI-generated video showing a Trump lookalike playing football, donning an Israel top, against the Lebanese national team.

Drones are said to appear in the video which begin dropping explosives on the players, with the man resembling Trump dying in the attack and images going on to show a young man wearing a Palestinian scarf.



New details about the security headaches neutralised by the FBI and the multi-agency command post IPCC, set up to coordinate global law enforcement during the World Cup, emerged last week.

It was revealed that football icon Lionel Messi was the target of a chilling terror plot involving suicide bombers.

A fanatic had vowed to blow up the Argentina star with a bomb vest during a match, according to the a police dossier.

Before Argentina’s match against Egypt he wrote on social media: “I’m going to walk into the Atlanta Stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs stuck to my body.”

Meanwhile, another man was said to have called Dallas airport just before a group-stage match between Argentina and Jordan.



He was reported to have said that he and two accomplices were headed for the city stadium with “home-made bombs and an AR-15 semi-automatic rifle”.

The double threat sparked a major hunt across the stadium by bomb specialists and sniffer dogs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Messi’s rival Cristiano Ronaldo was also an alleged victim of World Cup attack fears.

A FIFA employee raised the alarm after a “suspicious man” was asking for “details” about the Portuguese superstar’s World Cup accommodation.

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Araujo from Barcelona
Sports.content:
Liverpool have confirmed the signing of defender Ronald Araujo from Barcelona.

The deal is an initial loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract with Barca until 2031 last year, and also includes an option to buy for around £47.14m (€55m).

⁠Liverpool are not paying Barcelona a loan fee and will cover the entirety of Araujo's salary for the duration of the season-long loan. It is understood Araujo has taken a pay cut to facilitate the move.

Araujo, who will wear the No 33 shirt, told Liverpoolfc.com: "I can't wait to get started. I'm very, very happy.

"I'm excited to be here at this massive club with lots of history. I'm excited to meet my team-mates, excited to get started playing, and I'm very motivated and really up for getting going.

"I think it was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career. I think it was a move that was necessary for me to take. As soon as I heard that interest from Liverpool, everything went into action really, really quickly.

"As I say, I'm super-happy to be here and excited to get started. I'm glad about the interest and it was the right move at the right time."

The Uruguay international, who did not play at the World Cup due to injury, is expected to train with his new team-mates this week.

Araujo will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

Jacquet, a summer signing from Rennes, has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre-back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, leaving captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully-fit senior centre-back.

Image: Liverpool have signed Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan

Araujo, who can play at right-back and centre-back, moved from his native Uruguay in 2018 and made his Barcelona debut the following October, going on to play more than 200 games for the LaLiga side.

He was named as one of the club captains following the departure of Marc-Andre ter Stegen in January, but started only 11 LaLiga matches for the Catalan giants last season after an extended break from football in November 2025 to recover from what he later revealed was depression.

Why the Araujo deal works for Liverpool...

Liverpool had not been actively seeking out defensive reinforcements, their priority firmly on adding a wide forward, but this was a market opportunity that made sense for a number of reasons.

Ronald Araujo can play at centre-back or right-back, and, crucially, he was available on loan. This offered an appropriate solution to injury concerns that are deemed to be more short-term.

Liverpool have already committed £60m to signing Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes, with a view to him partnering Virgil van Dijk at centre-back.

However, it remains to be seen if he will be fit for the start of the season, as Liverpool take caution with his re-integration to competitive action following a shoulder injury that has kept him out since February.

A muscle problem for Joe Gomez, which will keep him out for the Premier League opener against Newcastle, has worsened the problem for new head coach Andoni Iraola, who by his own admission is slim on options at the back.

Araujo arriving on a temporary move alleviates that injury headache and adds a layer of experience to Liverpool's backline that is sorely missing. He has played more than 200 games for Barcelona after all.

There are understandable concerns around whether Araujo can turn around his struggles with form and fitness. Liverpool are not short on defenders with patchy injury records.

Liverpool are taking on a deal with an element of risk in that regard. But there is also a potentially big reward if Araujo does rediscover his best form thanks to the option to buy inserted in the deal worth around £47m.

At the peak of his powers, Araujo was being valued at around double that figure. Liverpool will hope to see his best in the Premier League, a division which is seemingly suited to his strengths.

How Liverpool were able to get Araujo

This is a deal that suits all parties. Liverpool require defensive cover amid injury worries around a number of players, while Araujo is not part of Hansi Flick's plans at Barcelona and is in need of a fresh start.

Araujo signed a new contract with Barcelona last year in January that reportedly put him among the club's highest earners. Six months earlier, he had been named Barcelona's vice-captain.

However, the Uruguay defender has since been unable to reach the heights that earned him such high status at Barcelona amid struggles with injury and his mental health.

Araujo wore the captain's armband as Barcelona celebrated becoming champions of Spain in May, but he had only played 24 times throughout the season.

Flick admitted when confirming the deal that Araujo was not suited to the way he wants to play and said the defender was excited about having the chance to move to a new environment.

Barcelona can now bring in a defender that Flick wants to work with, and Araujo has the opportunity to rebuild his career in the Premier League. If he performs, they will either earn a decent fee from Liverpool or his value will increase.

Sports.title: Sciver-Brunt helps Trent Rockets Women into Hundred final
Sports.content:
England all-rounder Nat Sciver-Brunt timed her introduction to perfection as 32 off 19 balls batting down the order secured Trent Rockets' progress to the final of The Hundred with a seventh successive victory.

Chasing 118 to win, the league leaders slipped to 10-3 against Southern Brave, the lowest powerplay score in the history of the competition, and even though passing 27 guaranteed their place in the final, the result remained in doubt.

Sciver-Brunt came in at number seven with the score on 66-5 and with 31 deliveries remaining - Ash Gardner having top-scored with 37 - and her experience avoided further drama.

She was run out going for a second which would have clinched victory, but Rockets still won with two balls to spare.

Southern Brave's 117-5 was built around their top order with Maia Bouchier scoring 38, Lizelle Lee 31 and Laura Woolvaardt adding 24.

They will get a second chance as they had already secured a place in the eliminator on Friday at The Kia Oval. Brave will discover their opponents on Tuesday, who will either be third-placed SunRisers Leeds or fourth-placed Manchester Super Giants who play each other at Emirates Old Trafford in their final group match.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Georgia Adams was run out in unfortunate fashion after Sarah Glenn fumbled a drive from Nat Sciver-Brunt and deflected the ball on to the stumps

Sciver-Brunt said: "I'm happy to be on the winning side. The wicket was a bit slow, and they bowled pretty well in the first half."

On batting down the order, she said: "It was a bit tactical and a bit injury management. We have got a lot of people in form and high on confidence. We have balanced our side nicely and building up to Sunday we sort of know what we need to do."

Sports.title: Rangers meeting Q&A: McInnes-Klopp compared, club failure admission & new signings update
Sports.content:
Rangers chairman Andrew Cavanagh believes the Ibrox side have become used to finishing second or worse over the last 15 years, and admits that failure had begun to "seep through" every corner of the club.

He was speaking at the club's shareholders' meeting, where it was also revealed they expect to add three to five more players this window, while Derek McInnes' appointment was compared to that of former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

It was also confirmed that Rangers have asked for an explanation over Hibernian's penalty in Sunday's 2-1 defeat as refereeing concerns were raised.

Image: Jim Gillespie was appointed Rangers chief executive in January

Chairman Andrew Cavenagh, Paraag Marathe of the San Francisco 49ers [who are part of the US consortium who took over the club], executive director Fraser Thornton and chief executive officer Jim Gillespie addressed a number of club issues and answered questions from the floor.

Here are some of the key takeaways...

On Derek McInnes

Image: Derek McInnes left Hearts to take charge of Rangers this summer

During the meeting, one shareholder asked why Derek McInnes, the man they wanted to ask questions to after a winless start to the season, was absent. Andrew Cavenagh explained that the panel had been arranged months ago and that McInnes' focus was at the training ground to help prepare the team.

When asked later about the process behind hiring McInnes, Jim Gillespie said you can either hire a 'Klopp' or a 'Guardiola' type. He said McInnes fitted the 'Klopp' type of being a manager who wants his teams to be agressive, on the front foot and attack the opposition.

During the summer when McInnes was appointed, Sky Sports News revealed he was the only candidate who was spoken to, and Gillespie defended that by adding he was the only option Ibrox chiefs felt "ticked all the boxes".

Cavenagh reminded shareholders that "culture eats strategy for breakfast", and when speaking about standards, revealed people had been late to training and not eating well. He went on to say he believed McInnes was the right man to address this.

On Recruitment

Image: Daisuke Yokota is one of nine summer signings at Rangers so far

Multiple shareholders raised concerns about player recruitment. However, Cavenagh defended the work in that department, adding he believes the squad is better than it was 12 months ago.

He admitted the team still requires between three and five more players before the end of the transfer window.

The meeting was called following a £16m share issue. Cavenagh confirmed that was needed to get the club through this "significant" summer transfer window. He added the club "will need more capital going forward".

Marathe insisted that they were "building something special" and referenced Youssef Chermiti's performances in the second half of last season, after initially struggling with the pressure of his price tag and playing for Rangers.

Image: Youssef Chermiti was injured in Sunday's defeat to Hibs, hours after it was revealed a bid had been rejected for the striker

On Chermiti, the club hierarchy were asked why he was selected for Sunday's match against Hibernian despite being the subject of a bid from Galatasaray. The striker was subsequently stretched off injured in the first half of that defeat.

It was explained that to accept a bid, Rangers need their value of the player to be met, and for sufficient time to reinvest those funds in the squad to make it equal or better. They reiterated there is no pressure to sell.

On Refereeing standards

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hibernian were awarded a first-half penalty in their 2-1 win at Rangers

Gillespie said that Rangers should be a leading club and want to have a constructive relationship with the Scottish FA and SPFL, while also holding both to account.

He was interrupted by a shareholder who said: "It's not working. It's been going on for years, nothing happens."

Marathe replied: "You're not wrong" but backed up Gillespie by saying, "we can't make it worse, we can't be in any more of what feels like a disadvantage".

Marathe added "he couldn't believe" the decision to award Hibernian a penalty in the first half of Sunday's match at Ibrox. Gillespie confirmed that Rangers have made contact with the Scottish FA to seek an explanation.

On Ibrox stadium

Image: Ibrox could be redeveloped with several proposals being considered

Marathe - who has overseen stadium expansion at Leeds United and the 49ers - discussed possible changes at Ibrox.

He said there would be news on that soon, while revealing one proposal is to lower the pitch at Ibrox, adding 5,000 to 6,000 seats.

It was also revealed, following fan surveys, a number of other ideas have been through a feasibility group and seen by architects.

Call for unity

Sports.title: Man City in Bouaddi talks and Chelsea's Fernandez also an option
Sports.content:
Man City are in ongoing talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Personal terms have been in place for a while with the 18-year-old as the clubs work to find an agreement.

As things stand, City do not consider talks with Barcelona for Rodri to be active after what they felt was a derisory opening offer, understood to be worth in the region of £40m.

The Spain captain is due to report back at City on Friday following his post-World Cup break. He has one year left on his deal and City would like him to renew.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Rodri linked with a move away from Manchester City, Sky Sports News reporter Ben Ransom discusses whether Ayyoub Bouaddi could be brought in to replace the midfielder

Sky Sports News understands Barcelona are considering their next offer for the 30-year-old.

Alongside Bouaddi, City are interested in several other midfielders, who could be turned to in the event of further sales. Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez is a player that they have on their list this summer.

Chelsea value the Argentina midfielder at £120m. He shared a strong working relationship with new City boss Enzo Maresca at Chelsea.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso discusses why Reece James will stay club captain under him and reveals he is looking forward to working with Enzo Fernandez

Who could leave Manchester City?

In terms of outgoings, City are aware of interest from Nottingham Forest in midfielder Tijjani Reijnders, who was signed from AC Milan last summer for £46m.

Mateo Kovacic is expected to stay and see out the final year of his deal at the Etihad.

Midfielder Nico Gonzalez has said he wants to stay, but it remains to be seen if his opportunities will improve under Maresca.

The City boss has said Omar Marmoush will decide his future at City, likening his situation to James Trafford's who has subsequently joined Leeds United.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the friendly between Manchester City and Atletico Madrid

Marmoush wants to play more minutes, and Maresca has left the door open for that to happen under him at City this season.

At this stage, there has been no fresh contact for Tottenham target Savinho, who wants to leave City to join Spurs.

Meanwhile, Vitor Reis is expected to stay with Man City this season and fight for a first-team place.

The 20-year-old Brazilian has impressed new manager Enzo Maresca on the Far East tour, after spending last season on loan at sister club Girona. He joined City 18 months ago for just under £30m.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki and England players Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson are due back at City on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Scotland, Netherlands criticise Cricket World Cup format changes
Sports.content:
Scotland and the Netherlands have criticised the restructuring of next year's 50-over World Cup, saying the changes "risk weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket".

At last month's board meeting in Edinburgh, the International Cricket Council announced the main part of the tournament in southern Africa will contain a dozen teams split into two groups of six.

There will still be 14 participants, but the tournament is slated to start with a preliminary round involving the three lowest-ranked qualifiers, with only one team progressing to the group stage.

A qualifying tournament will be held from February 22 to March 23 next year, with the winner going through to the main tournament and the second, third and fourth placed teams entering the first round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia are reigning 50-over champions having defeated India in the 2023 World Cup final

In a joint statement, Cricket Scotland and the Royal Dutch Cricket Association (KNCB) said they were "deeply disappointed" by the ICC's decision, announced less than 18 months before the tournament is due to start.

The statement said: "At a time when cricket is seeking to expand its reach, attract new audiences and strengthen its position on the international sporting landscape, reducing meaningful opportunities for emerging nations sends entirely the wrong message.

New Cricket World Cup format Round One: Teams 12, 13, 14 in round-robin ‘Super Series’

Teams 12, 13, 14 in round-robin ‘Super Series’ Top team progresses to Round Two

Round Two: Two groups of six teams (30 matches)

Two groups of six teams (30 matches) Top three teams in each group plus next best across both qualify

Round 3: Super 7 – Round robin (21 matches)

Super 7 – Round robin (21 matches) Top four teams progress to semi-finals

Semi-finals

Final

"We have significant concerns about both the impact of these changes and the process through which they have been introduced.

"The changes risk weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket, and only highlight the importance of strong governance, transparent decision-making and effective engagement with members."

Scotland and the Netherlands are currently 13th and 14th respectively in the men's ODI rankings.

Sports.title: 'Dubois has ingredients to replace Taylor as face of boxing'
Sports.content:
Caroline Dubois "has the ingredients" to succeed Katie Taylor as one of the biggest stars in boxing, according to Most Valuable Promotions partner Nakisa Bidarian.

Ireland's undisputed super-lightweight world champion Taylor, who turned 40 in July, is set to fight professionally for the final time in an undisputed world super-lightweight title fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on September 5.

A week earlier, lightweight world champion Dubois will seek to maintain her unbeaten record when she defends her WBC and WBO straps against American Amelia Moore, live on Sky Sports on the undercard of Chantelle Cameron's clash with Mikaela Mayer.

Bidarian told Sky Sports: "For me, the poster fighters of the sport have been Amanda Serrano and Katie Taylor, the two of them have been real trailblazers.

"It's sad to see that arc transition in September for Katie, I think Amanda probably has one more fight left after August 21.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Caroline Dubois' clash with Terri Harper for the WBC and WBO lightweight title.

"But women's boxing has never been stronger. It's a young sport, it became an Olympic sport in 2012 where Katie was the beneficiary, and she's created a storied career for herself.

"But we feel good about the future of this sport we feel like we have a roster of athletes. Caroline Dubois is one who I think has the ingredients of Katie Taylor, Amanda Serrano, Laila Ali, Christy Martin and Ronda Rousey all there.

"Of course, the sport's going to miss Katie, of course the ring is going to miss Amanda, but the sport is in a great place."

Salita says Shields is 'definitively No 1'

Undisputed heavyweight champion Claressa Shields is already "definitively" the No 1 fighter in women's boxing, according to her promoter Dmitry Salita.

Two-time Olympic gold medallist Shields has been an undisputed champion in the professional ranks in three weight classes, winning all 18 of her fights.

Asked about Shields' status in the sport amid Taylor's career coming to a close, Salita told Sky Sports earlier this year: "Katie Taylor is a historic figure in boxing, and I've said many times - personally and professionally - that I'm a fan of hers and what she has done for the sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Claressa Shields says Britain's Caroline Dubois could even eclipse her own achievements.

"That said, Claressa Shields is definitively the No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter in women's boxing today.

"What separates Claressa is not just what she's accomplished in the ring which already stands on its own but the totality of her impact.

"There is something more to being a bona fide superstar than simply being elite in the ring. There's an "it" factor. The ability to headline, to sell out arenas, to create moments, to carry events regardless of the opponent - and Claressa has that.



"She may be the first woman in the history of the sport consistently selling out major arenas regardless of opponent."

Will Shields vs Price happen?

Shields is dropping down from heavyweight in an attempt to become middleweight world champion once more, with the 31-year-old taking on Australian Kaye Scott in Atlanta this weekend.

The fight could be a precursor for a possible blockbuster with Britain's own world champion Lauren Price, who currently holds three of the four welterweight belts.

Talks have previously taken place over Shields and Price meeting at the middleweight, and despite an impasse in negotiations, Salita remains optimistic the fight can happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Claressa Shields discusses a potential fight with Lauren Price and insists that the pair could fight in both America and back in the United Kingdom for a rematch.

"When Claressa went to Wales, we believed we had the framework of a deal in place, and we're still operating in that spirit," Salita told Sky Sports last month.

"I believe we're close. Claressa is moving down to 160 pounds because she wants to make this fight happen. She's already accomplished so much, but she's always looking for the biggest global fights.

"Lauren is an outstanding fighter and an Olympic gold medallist. This is one of the biggest fights that can be made in women's boxing, and we're confident it will happen.

"Claressa has always done her part to make the biggest fights possible, and this is no different. We're ready to continue the discussions."

Sports.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
Sports.content:
Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”.

In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

The three confederations have started preliminary discussions about the organisation of new competitions along with Uefa’s repeated threats to boycott Fifa events. As things stand, next month’s under-20 women’s World Cup could take place without European teams and alternative options are being sought.

The letter is signed by the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, his AFC counterpart, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, and the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani. Efforts to unite around a suitable candidate to replace Infantino have stepped up since his privately backed plan was revealed and Montagliani is believed to be among the contenders.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” part of the letter reads. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it. When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

It strongly criticises Fifa’s response to the crisis, when a meeting between a small number of senior staff in Rabat was followed by an apology from Infantino that appeared not to show remorse for the scheme.

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment,” the letter says. “It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment – not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani consoles Lionel Messi after the World Cup final. He is believed to be interested in running for the Fifa presidency. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

The three presidents also call for an independent review, conducted by a body outside football, into the affair. Fifa had previously committed to presenting a full report to the Fifa Council at its next scheduled meeting.

The letter directly addresses concerns that countries may lose out on financial aid under a different leadership, saying it is “[not] about any member association losing the support it has earned, despite the fearmongering directed at our leadership to suggest otherwise”.

The letter concludes: “There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness … Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, with leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

51:14 Infantino hangs on by a thread and the overhaul at Newcastle | Football Weekly – video

Any candidates for the Fifa election must announce their bid by 18 November. The confederations are understood to consider all options in their push for Infantino to be replaced, provided they fit within Fifa’s statutes and governance framework.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

While the letter outlines the stances of the three confederations, and particularly their leaderships, the story is more complicated within individual member associations. Few outside Europe have been willing to come out publicly against Infantino and only a small minority have been tempted to recall the letters of support they had sent backing his re-election next March. The influential African and South American confederations, Caf and Conmebol, have come out backing Infantino in recent days.

A number of larger member associations have written to Infantino asking for a meeting where he would be required to explain his actions around the FFE scheme. No response has been received. Nor has Infantino been in touch with federations to address his leading role in the turmoil.

The confederations’ tripartite statement was followed by another joint release headed by World Cup hosts US Soccer and Canada Soccer, who along with the Caribbean Football Union and Central American Football Union also called for governance change at Fifa.

The four bodies comprise 40 of the 41 Concacaf members, with the outliers being the third World Cup hosts Mexico, who last Friday went public with their continued support for Infantino.

US Soccer had previously been silent and their willingness to condemn Fifa is significant, particularly as they are bidding to host the 2031 Women’s World Cup and also want to stage matches at the 2029 Club World Cup..

“U.S. Soccer, Canada Soccer, CFU (Caribbean Football Union) and UNCAF (Central American Football Union) stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens FIFA’s governance, transparency and accountability,” the statement read.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
A consortium including the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, is close to completing a deal for a 30% stake in Liverpool after months of talks with Fenway Sports Group. The investors are led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and who previously was a shareholder and director at Queens Park Rangers.

The Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is another member of the group who will pay in the region of £1.35bn. The deal is effectively agreed, but may take up to a month to complete.

Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (£190bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world, while Saverin is reportedly worth $32bn. This will be Bezos’s first investment in football, but he has previously looked into bidding for NFL franchises. The 62-year-old will receive equity as part of the deal, which Deloitte has advised on.

Bezos is the executive chair of Amazon having relinquished day-to-day control when he stepped down as chief executive five years ago. Under his leadership, the online retailer has diversified into being an entertainment provider and has bought numerous sports rights for its streaming service.

Amazon had live UK rights for 20 Premier League games each season for six seasons until the end of last year and broadcasts the Champions League in several European countries, as well as some NFL games in the US.

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 and have overseen two Premier League titles. FSG sold 3% of the club to the US private equity firm Dynasty Equity in 2023.

It has been a summer of change at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach, Mohamed Salah left on a free transfer and has joined Trabzonspor and Michael Edwards departed his role as chief executive officer at FSG.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 2: Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

The image of John McGinn hoisting aloft the Europa League trophy in Istanbul as the confetti cannons fired is crystallised in the minds of Aston Villa supporters, but less than three months on, plenty has changed since one of the club’s greatest days. Three major players from the starting lineup – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, two of whom scored – have exited, and another may follow if Arsenal make a serious play for the dependable Ezri Konsa.

A key trio of coaches have also left – the set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, assistant manager Pako Ayestarán and the influential individual coach, Antonio Rodríguez Saravia – but most importantly the common denominator and driver of Villa’s incredible rebirth remains in post. It is a good job Unai Emery enjoys a challenge. It has been a typically busy summer, with pre-season trips to Portugal, Indonesia and Hong Kong, plus the Super Cup against Paris St-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday and a friendly trip to Mönchengladbach to follow, but there is work to do if Emery is to repeat the feat of fourth place and break new ground, again, by securing Champions League qualification for successive campaigns.

After a terrible start, Villa edged over the line last season, but the landscape is unlikely to be so forgiving this time. Nobody played more minutes for Villa than Rogers and it was no surprise Villa’s alarming drop in form around spring coincided with Tielemans being injured. Villa need their replacements to work. João Gomes, a £38m buy from Wolves, looks a smart fit; the tigerish Brazil midfielder made the third-highest number of tackles in the division last season (107) and was fourth on the list for ball recoveries (194). Johan Manzambi is one of the game’s most exciting young talents, while Emery believes he can rehabilitate Alejandro Garnacho, who has joined on a season-long loan from Chelsea.

Only Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester City have amassed more Premier League points in the three-and-a-half years since Emery arrived, and while it would be foolish to write him off, every season his task seems to get that bit harder. He can still call on a core cast of reliable performers in Konsa, McGinn, Matty Cash, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins, while Boubacar Kamara’s return from injury this month is a timely boost. But it is hard not to wonder whether Villa have peaked.

Off-field picture

The response of a senior executive was telling when asked if qualifying for the Champions League makes life easier when it comes to meeting the financial rules. “Not easier but less difficult,” came the reply. Villa have since signed a lucrative shirt sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, worth about £20m per season, though Amnesty International warns Rwanda “is using sportswashing to deflect attention from its terrible human rights record”. Meanwhile, Villa Park’s makeover continues with the North Stand closed for the season, the stadium’s capacity falling to 37,000 during its redevelopment. The new-look stand will have a steel roof, modern facade and accommodate more than 12,000 fans - bringing the overall capacity past 50,000 supporters - and will be ready for 2027-28 and Euro 2028.

Owner-fan relationship

Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens will always be adored for putting Villa firmly back on the map, elevating them to become major Premier League players and, ultimately, as the people who gave Emery the keys to transform the club. Both joined the on-field celebrations in Istanbul in May, Sawiris with a claret-and-blue scarf around his neck. Michael Angelakis, chair of investment company Atairos and chief executive of Comcast, acquired a minority stake in 2023. The story goes that Sawiris, Egypt’s richest man, handed Emery a blank sheet of paper and asked him to design his vision when meeting the Basque for the first time in Madrid, at the home of the agent Jorge Mendes.

The manager

“He lives like a monk in a tracksuit,” was how Villa’s director of football operations and Emery’s right-hand man, Damian Vidagany, described the 54-year-old manager’s work ethic in the book Waking The Giant. During the season it is not unusual for Emery, who has an apartment in Birmingham city centre, to spend 12 hours a day at Villa’s Bodymoor Heath base, sometimes analysing footage on his laptop while on the exercise bike or treadmill, long after his players have gone. Emery’s squad have grown accustomed to long meetings, sometimes twice a day – one was held less than 12 hours after cementing their place in the Champions League after beating Liverpool in May, in preparation for Emery to clinch a record fifth Europa League title of his coaching career.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi looks pleased to be wearing the claret and blue. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

There were a few nerves at Villa as Manzambi illuminated Switzerland’s World Cup, concerns his price could balloon or that bigger fish may blow them out of the water. But Villa had done their homework and got a longstanding target over the line for a club-record £51m amid interest from rivals. Manzambi was on Villa’s radar long before he impressed against them for Freiburg in the Europa League final. Murat Yakin, the Switzerland head coach, described Manzambi as “a street footballer”, saying the 20-year-old’s humility and quality means he is capable of playing across the pitch. He played regularly as a No 8 in the Bundesliga and Emery is an admirer of his versatility.

Stat attack

Aston Villa scored 15 goals from outside the box last season. Seven teams had recorded more in one of the previous 17 Premier League campaigns, but no side in that period bettered their 8.4% shot conversion rate. As only 3.6% of attempts from this range are converted on average, Villa’s 2025-26 tally feels impossible to repeat.

Set for a breakthrough

It will be interesting to see if the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, son of former Plymouth and Shrewsbury forward Guy, can build on his encouraging pre-season form. Emery and his coaches are big fans of Madjo, a physical striker born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, so no wonder this month Villa welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) clearing Madjo to feature after Fifa rules prohibited him from playing after joining from Metz in a £10m deal in January. “English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo,” McGinn posted on social media. It has been a whirlwind 12 months for Madjo: he made his Ligue 1 debut last August aged 16, before scoring on debut for England Under-17s a few weeks later. Four goals in pre-season has led to a sense that his first competitive minutes for Villa are close.

World Cup impact

Amadou Onana, whose Villa career has been stop-start owing to injury, ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in Belgium’s last-16 win over the USA. Manzambi enjoyed a fine World Cup, even if his tournament also ended with a knee injury, ruling him out of Switzerland’s last 16 and quarter-final matches and delaying his Villa debut. Martínez made it to another final with Argentina. Konsa started every game for England before the semi-final against Argentina: his 72nd-minute introduction from the bench for Anthony Gordon widely pinpointed as a negative change that invited pressure.

Sports.title: Are Manchester United returning to relevance under Michael Carrick? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Manchester United finally seem to have something that resembles stability in the dressing room under Michael Carrick. I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.

There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. United don’t have to have an especially amazing season to play 15 more games this season than they did in 2025-26.

That’s not to say that Carrick won’t be successful. There was much that he did last season that was very impressive. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans bolster an area of the squad that desperately needed to improve. A left-back seems almost certain to arrive before the end of the month and there’s probably the need for one more high-class experienced central defender. It’s not clear what Marcus Rashford’s future is after his return from loan at Barcelona, but he has two years left on his contract and could add dynamism and finishing to the left side of the attack. It’s probably not a title-winning squad, but it’s certainly one that should qualify for the Champions League.

Two questions remain that will only be answered as the season goes on. First, Carrick himself: can he cope with the churn of two games a week, and operating with a squad that is at least as fatigued as their opponents? And second, where is the club psychologically? Part of the problem for United, a familiar trait of big clubs who have fallen from grace, is that they have got into a routine of failure, that no success can ever quite be trusted, and every setback is seen as a further example of the terminal decline (although just as damaging would be suddenly believing everything is fine if United were to win, say, their first three games of the season). Retaining clarity of thought and making realistic assessments are perhaps the greatest challenges for a club that has known greatness but is struggling to return to those heights.

What do you see the broader impact of the VAR changes that Fifa made this year being? Do you think that other soccer leagues will see the increasingly automated, faster but less human approach taken by Fifa this summer and choose to adopt it? (I am aware that the Premier League has already chosen to reject much of it) – Dennis.

The most notable changes implemented before the World Cup allowed VAR to review and overturn incorrectly awarded corner kicks, certain attacking fouls and clear mistakes relating to red cards given from a second yellow. The only one of these adopted by the Premier League is to allow VAR to overturn a second yellow leading to a red (VAR cannot recommend that a referee should award a second yellow that would lead to a red). If we have to have VAR, that seems reasonable enough; nobody wants to see a team incorrectly reduced to 10 men.

At the World Cup, the corner issue only rarely came up, but it always seemed slightly odd that incorrectly awarded goal kicks could not be turned into corners. Personally, I would scrap VAR, or at least this form of it, but if incorrect decisions can be corrected quickly and unobtrusively then they probably should be. I understand, though, why the Premier League, aiming for a “light touch” – good luck with that – would be resistant.

Greater use of VAR, though, seemed to be the direction of travel. I suspect relatively soon offsides will be almost fully automated, which probably makes sense so long as it’s almost instantaneous. Whatever doubts there may be about margins of error and frame rates, it’s still going to be more accurate than a 40-year-old running the line 30 yards away, peering through a thicket of players.

More significant is probably the Premier League’s adoption of regulations against timewasting: speeded-up substitutions, players who receive treatment having to remain off the field for 60 rather than 30 seconds, an outfield player having to be withdrawn for 60 seconds after a goalkeeper receives treatment, and a five-second clock on throw-ins and goal kicks. All should speed up the game and improve the spectacle. It’ll be interesting as well to see the level of tolerance for grappling in the box, particularly by attacking players, which was an area in which the Premier League seemed out of step with the rest of Europe last season.

Which of the Premier League’s promoted sides have the best chance of staying up, and why? – Nicholas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The achievements of Sunderland and Leeds last season, finishing seventh and 14th, will have heartened the promoted sides, but the truth is it will be extremely difficult for all three. Both those sides invested heavily in a way that is impossible for Coventry, Ipswich or Hull. It’s very hard to see how Hull, who were promoted unexpectedly, can survive. Coventry, perhaps, with the euphoria of their Premier League return and the Frank Lampard factor can give it a go, but their summer spending has been modest. Ipswich, with recent Premier League experience, have a chance and have made some intriguing signings in Daizen Maeda, Abdul Fatawu, Issa Diop and Chuba Akpom, but they’ve lost the manager who got them up, with Kieran McKenna opting for a break rather than another Premier League campaign. Gary O’Neil perhaps feels he has unfinished business, but if any of the promoted sides are to survive, they need another club to have a dreadful campaign.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Self-aggrandisement, backslapping and news from the past: it’s José time
Sports.content:
TUDUM …

“You don’t do a documentary with a guy who wins nothing,” parps José Mourinho during the trailer for his shiny, new Netflix film, although since 2017, his sole piece of silverware is the 2021-22 Tin Pot with Roma. And while his failure to win anything with Tottenham, Fenerbahce or Benfica didn’t exactly – on paper, at least – make him the most obvious candidate as the author of that opening quote, neither does he immediately feel like the best man to put Florentino Pérez’s Death Star back on course in Madrid.

And yet, here we are. Just like the cagey 1-0 wins at Chelsea after which Mourinho would come out and explain that his team played like Brazil ‘82, the Portuguese has willed the narrative into existence: Mourinho is, apparently, one of the best managers on the planet and his documentary, in which lots of retired talking heads will wax lyrical about his achievements 20 years ago, finds its way to your screens on Tuesday. And it will be lapped up. Partly because of the warm glow of nostalgia, partly because pretty much everyone in the northern hemisphere can’t bear to be outside in this heat, and partly because, for a good few years, Mourinho really was the best thing since Steffi Graf’s sliced backhand: at Porto, at Chelsea, at Inter and yes, even sometimes at Madrid.

Amid all the pomp, the self-aggrandisement and the backslapping, the documentary does include a few nice little nuggets from the past, namely Mourinho’s claim that he was in line to replace Alex Ferguson as manager of Manchester United in 2013, before tearfully pulling out at the last minute. “I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” he teases. “When I left Real Madrid [the first time], I signed with Manchester United to go to United after Sir Alex.” Ferguson, also part of the doc, adds: “He phoned me and he was crying. And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

While some cynics would argue that simultaenously signing a contract with United and giving Chelsea his word before spontaneously bursting into tears is exactly the sort of illicit chaos that Mourinho became famous for, few would argue that he remains absolutely box office, win, lose or draw. Roll on Real Madrid, then, famously a serene meadow of footballing tranquillity where ego, pressure and scrutiny do not dare to darken the door. Netflix would be wise to get the cameras back in; this season would make one heck of a documentary.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“It’s 15 years of frustration here at this club. Nobody knows that more than me … Every Rangers team is a byproduct of that frustration. The Rangers fans just want to see their team winning and so do I. And we will get there. I’m not going to ask the fans for more patience because I think the Rangers fans have been patient enough” – Derek McInnes there, now very much under the pump after his team slumped five points behind Celtic in the Scottish Premiership after just two games, losing 2-1 to Hibs at Ibrox.

View image in fullscreen Early-season dejection scenes at Ibrox. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA
