double quotation mark Having boycotted the Geopolitics World Cup due to my dislike of Fifa, Infantino, Trump, etc and therefore having nothing to write about, I’m now ready to pick up my quill and parchment once more. Even allowing for my team, Hearts’, disjointed recent hire and exits, I do think we have had incredibly bad luck in all our European draws. First it was Sturm Graz, now Benfica, and next, in Tin Pot, it seems likely we’ll get Rapid Vienna. I’ve actually heard of every one of these teams. Why couldn’t we have got some other made-up team from an even worse league than the Scottish Premiership? Or is getting out of Europe before the end of August the only thing that might help us in the league?” – Ken Muir.

double quotation mark I enjoyed the link to the Rivaldo article from 2002 (Friday’s Football Daily). It came complete with the quaint idea that a Serie A giant with Big Cup football could offer more wages than Spurs. Anyone under 30 would find the idea laughable” – Dave Lambley.

double quotation mark How beautiful St James’ Park was (Friday’s Memory Lane, full email edition). It really did remind me of the old Luigi Ferraris, where I spent nearly every Sunday in the early 80s. My mate was supporting the cyclists (Sampdoria) and me, of course, Genoa … we were taking each other to the home matches. I only went once to the one rebuilt for Italia 90 and found it so ugly and soulless. Some background in one of the local TV archives” – Giuseppe.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s letter o’ the day winner is … Dave Lambley, who gets some Football Weekly merch. Terms and conditions for our competitions can be viewed here.

Sports.title: Jordan Nobbs ready to complete wishlist with Newcastle WSL dream
Sports.content:
Jordan Nobbs says winning promotion to the Women’s Super League with Newcastle would fulfil her ambition for a club from the north-east to be in the top tier.

Nobbs, who has 71 England caps, was born in Stockton-on-Tees and believes women’s football in the region would benefit immensely from top-flight representation. ­Newcastle finished sixth in WSL2 last term, 11 points behind the title ­winners, ­Birmingham, and nine points off the playoffs, but this ­summer they have made their hopes clear with high-calibre signings from the top division, including the striker ­Martha Thomas from Tottenham and the Liverpool duo Leanne Kiernan and Gemma Evans.

Nobbs is clear about the ­target for the new campaign. “It is ­promotion. I know we said it last season [too],” she said. “I’ve always said things don’t happen overnight, [but] that is our goal. You have to say it out loud.

“Looking back on last season, we had some really good performances but nine draws, that’s too many points [dropped]. It’s just about focusing on finding a way to win. We’ve just got to build on the good stuff from last season, I don’t think we’re far off it.

“[Winning promotion with Newcastle], I’ve always said it would be job done. To get a northern team promoted … as I heard from Newcastle I was like, that is exactly what I want to do. In the WSL, I’d ticked as much as I possibly could, so to get a north‑east team, which we all had to leave back in the day, promoted would be an achievement I would love.”

Nobbs began her career with Sunderland and broke into their team in the old top flight, but moved to ­Arsenal when the ­WSL was launched in 2011 and Sunderland’s application to join the breakaway division was rejected. That led to a successful team also including Nobbs’s future England teammates Lucy Bronze and Lucy Staniforth breaking up.

Sunderland did compete in the top tier between 2015 and 2018, but north-east representation in the WSL has been sparse, so Nobbs is pleased to see investment in recent years at Newcastle as well as their WSL2 rivals, who were taken over in June by Bay Collective.

“It’s been a long time coming, but it was something us ­northerners have always wanted,” Nobbs said. “We don’t want the north-east to fizzle out. We want to show the players that have come from there and developed there.

“It’s definitely grown in the right ­direction now, which is what we wanted. But the big stepping stone would be getting into the WSL. That would be where we really put the north-east back on the map and I’d love to be a part of that.”

The 33-year-old has enjoyed her role in Tanya Oxtoby’s setup at Newcastle after joining them last July. “With Villa I played a lot of a deeper role and [now] I really love being back in my high position, scoring goals, assisting and [I’m] in my happy place. I feel like I found that little spark again [last season] that was nice.”

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille valueing Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and open their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

Barcelona are confident of landing Rodri from City, but will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint-Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester teenager Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of a deal for the 18-year-midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Marcus Rashford has joined United at their County Kildare training camp following the England forward’s post-World Cup break.

The 28-year-old has spent the last season and a-half on loan at Barcelona and Aston Villa, respectively, due to a breakdown in his relationship with the club executive and the former head coach, Ruben Amorim. Relations have now eased and Rashford is focused on working under the manager, Michael Carrick, although he could still leave before the end of the window

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of messing with his mental health after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, are understood to have agreed four-year contracts with the option of a further 12 months. They are expected to have medicals on Monday.

McNeil, who has entered the final year of his Everton contract, appeared to be moving to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season.

They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League, but then pulled out. McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, wrote an emotional post on Instagram saying there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been affected.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

Johnson has been disappointing since moving to Palace, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given he signed a four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid, but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.

Palace are also finalising a deal to sign Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m. The Israel right-back had his medical on Sunday and is expected to sign a five-year contract. The 21-year-old’s move to Internazionale broke down last month after he failed a medical.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish told fans would love perfect transfer to Premier League club
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor has insisted the majority of Aston Villa fans would welcome Jack Grealish back at the club.

The 30-year-old is facing an uncertain future, having returned to Manchester City this summer after Everton opted not to take up the £50million buy option in his loan deal.



4 Grealish grew up as a Villa fan and came through the ranks at the club to captain them Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Having fallen out of favour at the Etihad Stadium before moving to the Toffees, it is currently unclear whether Grealish will be given a chance to prove himself under new boss Enzo Maresca.

This has fed speculation that the Englishman could leave permanently this summer, with City keen on selling him as he is entering the final year of his contract.

While talkSPORT understands Grealish is drawing interest from Saudi side Al Hilal, he would prefer to stay in the Premier League.



Another potential next destination which has been mooted is former club Aston Villa, five years on from his £100million exit.

Grealish joined the Citizens from boyhood club Villa in 2021 for a then British record transfer, having established himself as a cult hero during his time at the club.



After rising through the youth ranks at Villa Park, the forward went on to become captain, leading his team back to the Premier League in 2019 after a three-year absence, before starring for them in next two years in the top flight.

A move could also be advantageous for Villa, who are keen to strengthen their forward line after losing star man Morgan Rogers to Chelsea in a new British record £117m move.



Happy homecoming?

While Grealish left Villa fans heartbroken when he left for City five years ago, talkSPORT host and club icon Agbonlahor has insisted he would be welcomed back with open arms should he choose to return.

Agbonlahor said: "I would love him to come back, but it's a question for if Jack wants to come back, it's a question if the manager wants Jack.

“I think he'd love to come back to Villa, yeah. He's a Villa fan. He loves Aston Villa. I would have him back tomorrow.

4 Grealish may find himself further down the pecking order at City after returning from Everton Credit: Getty



4 Grealish captained Aston Villa to victory in the Championship Play-Off Final in 2019, sealing the club's return to the Premier League Credit: Getty - Contributor

Despite tipping Grealish for a homecoming, Agbonlahor admitted Villa boss Unai Emery may have different plans for his team, pointing to the recent loan signing of Alejandro Garnacho.

He continued: "But has the manager got other ideas for that left-hand side? We are short in that position, 100 per cent.

“I'd take Jack over Garnacho any day. All day, every day of the week.”



Continuing to state a case for Grealish to return, Agbonlahor insisted that he left Villa on good enough terms to be welcomed back.

That is despite the England international being booed by his old fans on his return to Villa Park with Man City in 2021.

On Grealish's 2021 exit, Agbonlahor continued: “It was no problem. There was a release clause in the contract that he left. I think the majority of them would [take him back], yeah.

4 Grealish could be given a chance to impress new Man City boss Enzo Maresca Credit: Getty



“I reckon 90-95 per cent of Villa fans would say yes. If he's going to make our team better, he's a Villa fan. And let's not forget, he didn't leave in a bad situation. He got the club £100million.

“They used that money elsewhere. Exactly. So I think it would be an amazing signing.

“Just down to the manager, if he wants him, it'll be interesting.”

Despite this, Agbonlahor admitted it remains a possibility that Grealish could yet stay at Man City, if he is given a second chance under new boss Maresca.

He added: “I think there's a chance that he does stay at Man City as well. Because he knows Maresca, Maresca was a coach under Pep [Guardiola] as well. So he knows him. He could stay, yeah.”

Sports.title: Why Mohamed Salah has joined Trabzonspor – and it’s not just about the 50 per cent wage rise
Sports.content:
Why Mohamed Salah has joined Trabzonspor – and it’s not just about the 50 per cent wage rise

Mohamed Salah had plenty more reasons to join Trabzonspor rather than just a bumper pay rise, says talkSPORT's Andy Brassell.

Salah completed a free transfer to the Turkish club last Tuesday, penning a two-year deal.

3 Trabzonspor is the seventh different club Salah has played for Credit: AFP

It is an impressively lucrative move for Salah as he will receive a monster salary of £14.5million a season.

Salah stands to rake in even more funds as he will earn a 20 per cent share of products sold in his name along with conditional bonuses.

Despite the dizzying deal, European football expert Brassell believes there was far more to Salah's decision-making process ahead of joining Trabzonspor.

Andy Brassell explains why Mohamed Salah joined Trabzonspor

"Clearly, he could have made more in Saudi Arabia," Brassell said on talkSORT's Trans Euro Express.

"But clearly, he never really seemed to show any inclination to go out there. And for them to be able to sign an Arab superstar, for the Saudi Pro League it would have been absolutely huge. I suspect that's part of it as well.

"Nicolas Anelka spoke in the past about when he went to Fenerbahce, a huge part of it was at that point in his life, he wanted to live and play in a Muslim country. I suspect that's at least part of it for Mo Salah as well.

"But for so many players, and we're seeing prime age players, players younger than Mo Salah going to big Turkish Super Lig clubs. It's the fact that you can get paid better than you can in western Europe without having to leave the competitiveness of European football and UEFA club competitions, I think that's really key as well."

This summer has proven especially eye-catching when it comes to younger players moving to big Turkish clubs.

One example is former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood, who joined Fenerbahce from Marseille for approximately £38m at just 24 years of age.

Fenerbahce have also snapped up centre-back Nathan Ake while Galatasaray are targeting Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli, who is 25 years old.

3 Despite being 34 years old, Salah is keen to prove he still has what it takes to compete Credit: Getty

No matter their age, all will be vying for the Turkish Super Lig title.

It is a trophy Galatasaray have had a vice-like grip on, having won four consecutive league crowns.

How Mohamed Salah is hoping to inspire Trabzonspor to former glories

Prior to Galatasaray's run, the last team to have had the league title in their possession was Trabzonspor, who accomplished the feat in 2021/22.

Aside from their recent success, Trabzonspor boasts a fan base unlike any other, something which Salah has already experienced as thousands turned out to welcome him at the airport and even more attended his unveiling at their stadium.

"They're passionately supported out there on the Black Sea in a city that leaves and breathes football, which must be part of it as well," Brassell continued.

"I think even for experienced players, the minute you get off the plane and see all the fans, it's a pinch-me moment.

3 Salah received a hero's welcome at Papara Park Credit: Getty

"You get to play in busy stadiums that are so, so passionate in a level that even coming from the Premier League, you just can't understand. That is a huge part of it."

It's not just the Turkish Super Lig that Salah and his new teammates will be eyeing off.

Thanks to their third-place finish last term, Trabzonspor qualified for the Europa League play-off round and will face either Hungarian side Ferencvaros or Polish outfit Gornik Zabrze.

Galatasaray was the first and remains the only Turkish club to have won the competition, doing so in 2000.

But the marquee signing of Salah, who scored over 250 goals for Liverpool, could be the perfect tonic to help Trabzonspor win their first European trophy in history.

Sports.title: Barcelona set to avoid extra payment to Man City as Ferran Torres closes in on £42m transfer
Sports.content:
Barcelona set to avoid extra payment to Man City as Ferran Torres closes in on £42m transfer

Barcelona are set to avoid paying an add-on fee to Manchester City as he closes in on a £42million move to Paris Saint-Germain.

Torres joined Barcelona from Man City back in January 2022 for an initial €55million, signing a contract until the summer of 2027.



2 Torres is out of contract at the Camp Nou next summer Credit: Getty

But the versatile forward has emerged as an option for the back-to-back Champions League winners.

Should the deal be completed, it might also open up a potential departure for Bradley Barcola, with Liverpool very keen.

The cost of keeping Torres

Barcelona have already paid Man City €10m in add-ons, but they’ll have to pay around a further €8m if the Spain international extends his contract at the Camp Nou, The Athletic report.



As such, LaLiga champions Barca are said to be erring against offering Torres a new contract.

And with the 26-year-old not becoming a free agent until next summer, he would command a fee in the current transfer window.



Torres scored the winner in the World Cup final for Spain as he slammed home late on to ensure La Roja beat Argentina at the MetLife Stadium.

It made Spain two-time world champions and ensured Torres' name is in history forever.



The former Valencia man made 49 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions last season, scoring a career-best 21 goals.

That being said, he endured a 14-game goal drought between January and April and lost the starting place he’d gained from Robert Lewandowski.

With that in mind, Barcelona may not be overly concerned about parting ways with him this summer.

Torres has found the net 65 times in his four-and-a-half years at Barcelona, winning three LaLiga titles and a Copa del Rey.



He previously won the Premier League title and EFL Cup in his only full campaign at Man City, as well as reaching the Champions League final.

2 Torres joined Andreas Iniesta in becoming just the second man to score for Spain in a World Cup final

Spain's super-sub

As far as goalscoring goes, he’s fared better in international football, striking 25 times in 65 caps since making his senior Spain debut six years ago.

Part of the squad that went all the way at Euro 2024, Torres mostly featured as a substitute at the 2026 World Cup, and he came off the bench again to win the World Cup for his country.



A changing of the guard

Barcelona have already offloaded two players for fees this off-season, with goalkeeper Inaki Pena and attacking midfielder Ansu Fati joining Panathinaikos and Monaco respectively.

Meanwhile, veteran striker Lewandowski has left following the expiry of his contract, joining MLS side Chicago Fire.

In terms of inbound business, Anthony Gordon has been the sole signing so far, joining for £70m.

Arriving from Newcastle, the England star became only the third English player to sign for Barcelona since the Second World War.



Gordon's international teammate Marcus Rashford spent last season on loan at the Camp Nou, but his move has not been made permanent, with Barcelona signing Karim Adeyemi.

Sports.title: Endrick told why he should reject Aston Villa to sign for European giant
Sports.content:
Endrick told why he should reject Aston Villa to sign for European giant

Endrick has been told to turn down a loan move to Aston Villa in favour of joining Roma.

talkSPORT understands the Villans are considering bringing the Real Madrid starlet to Villa Park on loan, having found playing time hard to come by since moving Spain in 2024.

4 Endrick could make his first step in English football this summer Credit: Getty

Endrick spent the second half of last season on loan at Lyon from the Spanish giants, and has since returned to the club this summer.

The 20-year-old scored eight goals and added eight assists in 21 appearances for Lyon during his loan spell.

But he could seal another temporary switch away from the Santiago Bernabeu this summer, with the recent arrival of Yan Diomande likely to push Endrick further down the pecking order.

Villa, who are looking to bolster their attacking options as they prepare for Champions League football in the upcoming season, are among the clubs considering offering him a shot at regular game time.

Unai Emery's side have already had to deal with some high-profile departures - namely Morgan Rogers' British record transfer to Chelsea and Youri Tielemans leaving to join Manchester United.

But Villa aren't the only side keen on Endrick, with Serie A side Roma also interested in snapping him up on a short-term basis.

The bigger picture

While a loan move to Aston Villa would give Endrick an opportunity to prove himself in the Premier League, European football expert Andy Brassell believes this may not be best for his development.

He insisted that the physicality of the Premier League wouldn't best prepare the Brazilian for a long-term career at Real Madrid, claiming a move to Italy with Roma could benefit him more.

Asked if a move to Villa could be a possibility, he told talkSPORT: “It could be, it shouldn't be. I'm not sure it's in his best interests at this point in time.

"Of course he was loaned to Lyon in Ligue 1 for the second half of last season. And he did pretty well. I think it's easy to look at it from a distance and say he did really well. Pretty well is the truth. He had some really good bits, he had some difficult bits."

4 Emery will need squad depth this season as Villa look to compete in Europe Credit: Getty

4 Endrick's strong run of form for Lyon saw him named in Brazil's World Cup squad Credit: Getty

Brassell continued: "He's got everything to be a superstar.

“In terms of what you can do on the pitch, it's not there yet. I think ideally he probably would have gone back to Lyon for a year - that would have been good for him.

“Real Madrid obviously wanted [Jose] Mourinho to have a look at him. And now because of the signing of Diomande and many other forward options that they've got, they've got to clear the decks. And they will loan Endrick out, it looks like.

"I think of the options out there, Roma is the one that makes the most sense. They're looking for wired players.

"Serie A is a subtle step up from where he was in the second half of last season. He can continue to progress and he'll play loads.

“I just think if he goes to Villa, it's not really training him for LaLiga. He'll get kicked loads and he probably won't play every game."

4 There were high hopes for Endrick when Real Madrid agreed to sign him as a 16-year-old in 2022 Credit: Rex

Options

While Brassell felt a loan to Aston Villa could hinder Endrick's long-term future at Real Madrid, he admitted the Brazilian could put himself in the shop window for a permanent move next summer by impressing on loan in the Premier League.

On a potential loan move to Villa, he added: "I don't really see what the benefit is for Real Madrid there, unless they're now moving towards selling him. Because I think what would be the smart thing.

“If they're looking to selling him, of course the most lucrative market is the Premier League.

"So you put him out there, if he looks like the business in the Premier League, don't attach a buy option for Villa. Then you can sell him for what you want at the end of the season.

“But of course they might need an obligation, they might need money in the short term, because they've been out there spending a lot of money. Certainly in terms of contracts, they'll be spending loads more.

“I just hope he gets somewhere where he's going to play and be an important player.”

Sports.title: Chelsea told to make move for £35m-rated Premier League full-back
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea player Andy Townsend believes that Djed Spence would be a very good addition for the Blues this summer.

Spence looks set to leave Tottenham Hotspur with Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson fighting out at left-back and Pedro Porro the obvious choice at right-back.

3 Spence enjoyed a standout World Cup for England Credit: Getty

Liverpool have also been linked with a move for the versatile full-back, but talkSPORT understands the Reds are yet to make any move, with the player understood to be keen on a move.

Chelsea are yet to be linked with a swoop for their rivals' player amid talk of a £35million fee being enough for Tottenham to part ways.

But Townsend believes that Chelsea could do a lot worse than bringing in Spence, who shone for England at the World Cup.

Either at left-back or right-back, he was one of the Three Lions' standout players, and after losing Marc Cucurella and with Malo Gusto being available, Townsend thinks a move for Spence is sensible.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast with Jeff Stelling, he said: "I don't know what he would cost because of how well he did at the World Cup.

"Has that inflated his price tag unreasonably? I genuinely haven't got a clue.

"If Cucurella is going to Real Madrid for over £60million, I would have thought Djed Spence at £40million, something around that figure, would be a decent acquisition.

"It wouldn't do them any harm to have someone who is still looking to improve as a player, who is all ears and wants to get better.

"He is now showing what he is capable of, so that wouldn't be a bad piece of business."

Spence's future

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs understands that the 26-year-old has been offered to Liverpool and Manchester United by the player's agency.

3 Xabi Alonso has a pretty bloated squad, but full-back cover isn't massive Credit: Getty

However, neither side is yet to nibble on the opportunity.

Spence is seeking regular first-team football, which isn't guaranteed under Roberto De Zerbi. Tottenham aren't in Europe this year, so there are fewer games for the full-back to be involved in.

What else do Chelsea need to do?

Chelsea have already splashed a lot of money this summer for new manager Xabi Alonso. Morgan Rogers has joined in a British record transfer from Aston Villa.

The defence has been strengthened with the arrivals of Maxence Lacroix and Marco Palestra. Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck have added some experience as well.

However, Townsend feels as if a new goalkeeper would be something to look at.

The Blues have allowed Filip Jorgensen to depart and join sister club Strasbourg on loan.

There were links to Porto keeper Diogo Costa, but Chelsea have informed talkSPORT they are not true.

3 Sanchez is set to be Chelsea's number one Credit: Getty

On Sanchez and the goalkeeper situation, Townsend said: "Robert Sanchez is one of those goalkeepers that Monday to Friday, he must be unbelievable.

"He must be plucking them out of the top corner and making saves from all angles - he must be brilliant.

"Everyone at the club thinks there is a proper goalkeeper there, whereas most of us are waiting for a rick or a lapse in concentration.

"You are just waiting for him to scupper all of the good work that clearly he can do.

"I would have thought that if Chelsea want to win the league, and I am sure they will want to again at some point, they are going to have to upgrade.

"But they obviously haven't seen anything they really fancy, so they are going to continue to go with Sanchez.

"He's got all of the profile that you need to be a top goalkeeper, but it is that carelessness in his game that tends to have everybody talking about that rather than the good saves."

Sports.title: Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh gives statement as he pulls out of running to buy Derby County
Sports.content:
Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh gives statement as he pulls out of running to buy Derby County

A deal that would see Saudi boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh buy Derby County has fallen through.

The Championship club confirmed on Monday that Lion Sport, a consortium linked with Alalshikh, have opted not to proceed with the purchase despite approval from the Independent Football Regulator and the EFL.



4 Alalshikh has transformed boxing since his involvement in the sport, but his wait to break into English football goes on Credit: Getty

Derby also said that they are not open to any fresh offers for the foreseeable.

Derby confirm deal is off

"The club can confirm discussions with Lion Sport to buy a controlling interest in Derby County will no longer proceed," the Rams said in a statement.

"The purchase process had been sanctioned by both the Independent Football Regulator and the EFL, notification of which the club received last week.



"However, today the club received notice that Lion Sport no longer wanted to continue with the purchase.

"For the benefit of any doubt, the club is now off the market and will continue to operate under the loyal, committed and unwavering support of Clowes Developments.



"Our preparations continue for the new EFL season, beginning against Charlton Athletic on Saturday. The club will offer no further comment."

Derby have been out of the Premier League since 2008 when they recorded the worst season in Premier League history.



They managed to accumulate just 11 points and have been into League One since then as well.

Alalshikh's wait to break into English football goes on but he has involved himself in the sport before, though.

He has owned Spanish club Almeria and Egyptian side Pyramids FC in the past but has been looking to invest in EFL clubs.

4 It's back to square one with regards to a change of ownership for Derby Credit: Shutterstock



Alalshikh gives statement

Shortly after Derby's statement, Alalshikh explained why the deal didn't happen as he cited the season already beginning and a lack of preparation as a result for not going through with the deal.

He also refused to rule out any future attempts to buy Derby.

"I would like to thank everyone at Derby County Football Club, and everyone involved in this process for all their hard work over the past few months," Alalshikh said in a statement.

"We understood that the IFR (Independent Football Regulator) process takes time and fully respect the importance of that, but unfortunately with the season already started, it would leave us with no time to prepare the team or the club for the season ahead.

"After careful consideration, we don't feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future.



"I personally wish the team and club every success for the season ahead."

4 Turki has been previously linked with a move to buy Championship clubs Millwall and Southampton Credit: Getty

Alalshikh's wealth

The latest reports suggest that Alalshikh is worth $2.8billion, and he has accumulated that wealth from various means.

He is the chairman of the Saudi General Entertainment Authority and is heavily involved in boxing.



Alalshikh is one of the leading figureheads in Riyadh Season, which has transformed boxing and put on some of the biggest fights in history.

He is widely seen as the mastermind behind the 'Battle of Britain' between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

A new boxing venture between he and Dana White and Frank Warren known as Zuffa Boxing has been brought into existence with big plans.

Alalashikh is also a close advisor to the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia, Mohammed bin Salman.



4 Alalshikh doesn't lack ambition or money Credit: Getty

Jordan advises Alalshikh to buy Owls

talkSPORT's Simon Jordan revealed last year that he advised Alalshikh on which English club to go for, telling him to buy Sheffield Wednesday.

Speaking about that conversation in 2025, Jordan said: “If I was buying a football club and I was really motivated and had your kind of dough, I would buy Sheffield Wednesday."

Expanding on that, Jordan said: “I told him that. We’ll see what they do; they are captains of their own ship, aren’t they?



“Be careful what you wish for. We’ve already got enough foreign investment in our football clubs, but if this is the direction of travel, that’s the way I’d go.

"It’s a big football club. There’s a reason why Hillsborough got used up to a point, for FA Cup semi-finals.

“But I’ve been to that club, I’ve watched it, I’ve seen the fan base. I know the Saudis can look across the city at Sheffield United and think their mate who owns that football club hasn’t had the greatest of times over there, but I think it’s a powerhouse."

“You buy a powerhouse like Sheffield Wednesday that’s in Yorkshire, not just Sheffield, that could be garnered and pushed forward, no disrespect to [current owner, Dejphon] Chansiri, but somehow or another he’s managed to steal defeat from the jaws of victory."

Sports.title: What time is Carabao Cup second round draw? Chelsea and Tottenham enter with draw split into sections
Sports.content:
What time is Carabao Cup second round draw? Chelsea and Tottenham enter with draw split into sections

The Carabao Cup has kicked off the new English football season and the second round draw is coming up tonight.

An action-packed summer weekend of cup football has seen teams progress or crash out early and the focus will now shift to the next round's draw.



3 The journey to lifting the Carabao Cup trophy is officially underway Credit: Getty

For successful clubs in Round One, they could well be handed a huge tie in the second round, as some Premier League giants join.

Both Chelsea and Tottenham are going to be in the Round Two draw, having not qualified for Europe last season.

There are also another nine Premier League sides getting involved, potentially being put at risk of a major upset.



Here's all you need to know about the Carabao Cup draw...

When is the Carabao Cup second round draw?

The draw for Round Two of the Carabao Cup will take place on Monday, August 10.

The ball picking will commence at approximately 7:20pm.

It will be held before Plymouth Argyle face local rivals Exeter City in what is the final game of the first round.



Second round ties will be played on the week commencing August 24.

3 Xabi Alonso is set to find out his first Carabao Cup opponent as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty

How to follow the Carabao Cup draw

The second round draw will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football in the build-up to the Devon derby.



It will be part of their match coverage from Home Park.

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also be right across the latest.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



Which Premier League clubs are joining?

There are 11 Premier League clubs joining the Carabao Cup at the second round, with nine others not yet involved.

Chelsea and Spurs are among the 11 sides without European football, with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest in the same boat.

Leeds also won't be playing in Europe, along with Everton, Brentford, Fulham, and newly-promoted Coventry, Ipswich and Hull.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Manchester United are four of the nine clubs joining the Carabao Cup in the third round.



3 Tottenham are entering the competition at the second round after a poor last season Credit: AFP

How does the second round draw work?

The Carabao Cup second round follows the same format as the first round, splitting the competition into regions.

Teams are split into Northern and Southern sections.

So, they will be drawn against a club that are in their region.

This will then change for the third round, when all teams can be drawn against each other no matter their location.

Sports.title: Harry Kane told contract decision means major goal record will never be beaten
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has been warned signing a new deal with Bayern Munich could prevent him from making Premier League history.

The England captain's current contract with the German giants expires next summer.

4 Kane looks set to stay in Germany for the foreseeable future, but it may mean the Premier League goal record is out of reach Credit: Getty

However, he is expected to sign an extension having joined Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023 for £86m.

Barcelona and Al Hilal both previously made enquiries regarding Kane's availability earlier this summer, but the 33-year-old now looks set to prolong his stay in the Bundesliga.

The news will delight Bayern fans given it comes after he won a third successive golden boot, with his overall tally for the club now at 146 goals in 147 appearances.

Record in doubt

His decision to remain with the club also delays any potential return to the Premier League in the future.

Kane is the division's second leading scorer of all-time thanks to his 213 top-flight goals for Spurs.

He trails record holder Alan Shearer by just 47 strikes, with the legendary striker scoring 260 goals in 441 Premier League outings for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United.

talkSPORT's Darragh MacAnthony believes that record will now be out of reach for Kane even if he returns to England in the future.

Discussing his imminent contract extension with co-presenter Max Scott, the Peterborough United chairman explained: "Bayern Munich don’t need money, so what are you going to pay to get their No.9 and probably the Ballon d’Or winner this year out the building, even at 34 or 35 years old?

"Spurs aren’t going to pay £60-70million - giving [Bayern] their money back, are they? So I’m not shocked he’s extended.

"I always thought Kane would come back and play his final couple of years in the Premier League.

"I’m not sure he can break [Shearer’s record) at that age. He would probably need three or four seasons to do that, but I did think he’d come back to Spurs. I thought he'd end his career there.

4 Shearer is the Premier League's top scoring player of all time and his record is safe if Kane stays away, MacAnthony thinks Credit: Getty

"He’s one of them that’s defying the odds. Father time hasn’t caught up with him, he’s just had his most productive season and I do think he should win the Ballon d’Or."

Will Kane break the record?

When told Kane is just 47 goals short of Shearer's record, MacAnthony added: "He could do it if he comes back in two years.

"He’d need four seasons, at that age you’d be doing 10 a year. He won’t be breaking that record (if he extends) so it’s a shame really.

"We should never have lost him. The Premier League should never have lost Harry Kane, one of the most prolific goalscorers of our generation."

4 Kane scored 213 Premier League goals for Spurs before his move to Bayern for £86m Credit: Getty

4 The Ballon d'Or appears to be Kane's to lose at this stage Credit: talkSPORT

Kane is fresh from scoring 61 goals in 51 matches for Bayern across all competitions last season, launching himself into Ballon d'Or contention.

He continued his form into the World Cup, scoring six times for England as they finished third overall.

Kane to upset talkSPORT's Tottenham fans

DJ Majestic would love to have seen Kane back 'home'.

Using his show, he explained to talkSPORT listeners how history could have been made.

"[Manager] Roberto De Zerbi says to him: 'Look, it's one season without European football, which allows you to have a bit more of a rest after a long season and a World Cup, it gives you the focus of scoring goals in the Premier League, you don't have to play in the League Cup.

"You are that close to Alan Shearer's record. If you have a good season this year, scoring 20+, which is very possible to do, you could become a Bundesliga champion, England's greatest goalscorer, Tottenham's greatest goalscorer and possibly the Premier League's greatest ever goalscorer.

"This is Harry Kane's legacy set in stone. People can't say he hasn't won anything, he's gone and done that. Now he can come home and push Spurs on.

"Come on Harry, it's time to come home, it's good for you, it's good for us, it's good for Bayern, let's do it."

Sports.title: City still want Bouaddi, West Ham interested in signing free agent Jamie Vardy as striker prepares to return to England - and Newcastle talks with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg hit stumbling block: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

City not giving up on Bouaddi

Manchester City are continuing discussions with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is keen to join City now rather than wait another season, which was Lille's preference, and the clubs are working towards agreement on a fee.

City still want another midfielder for when Rodri joins Barcelona with talks ongoing over a fee for the Spain captain.

Tottenham are continuing to monitor developments with Omar Marmoush and Savinho while Nottingham Forest want Tijjani Reijnders.

City and Southampton have agreed a season-long loan deal for Divin Mubama, as revealed by Daily Mail Sport. The 21-year-old forward spent last season on loan at Stoke City making 28 appearances in all competitions prior to damaging ankle ligaments in January.

The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is keen to join Man City this summer

Chelsea line up LA Galaxy youngster

Chelsea are close to finalising a deal for 16-year-old LA Galaxy midfielder Vicente Garcia.

The deal is expected to be worth £2.25m plus add-ons and Garcia would join Chelsea when he turns 18 in 2028.

Hojbjerg talks with Toon break down

Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, became a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

The Denmark star is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested

Newcastle winger Murphy set for Kaiserslautern

Newcastle United defender Alex Murphy is on the verge of a season-long loan move to Kaiserslautern.

The Republic of Ireland U21 international, who can play centre-back and left-back, is having a medical ahead of joining the Bundesliga 2 club.

Liverpool's Morrison wanted by Groningen

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is attracting interest from FC Groningen among other clubs. The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international will be allowed to leave on loan.

Morrison, who started out at Manchester United, made his international debut in June against Guinea.

Tottenham winger off to Belgium

Tottenham winger Yang Min-hyeok is in talks to join Belgian side Westerlo. The 20-year-old, who joined Spurs in 2025, has had loan spells with QPR, Portsmouth and Coventry City since. The South Korea international is expected in Belgium today for his medical.

Hammers knocked back in Parrott pursuit

West Ham have had their opening bid for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott rejected.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Hammers made their opening offer of around £15million over the weekend but it is likely to take a Championship record fee of £17.5m to get their man. They are now formulating a new offer.

RB Leipzig have also contacted Alkmaar in recent days but the Hammers are further advanced.

West Ham are exploring a move for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson and have made an approach for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Tigers turned down in Vipotnik pursuit

Hull have had a bid rejected by Swansea for striker Zan Vipotnik.

The Premier League side's offer is understood to have fallen well short of Swansea's valuation of last season's Championship top scorer.

Palace keen on Khalaili

Crystal Palace's move for Union Saint-Gilloise right wing-back Anan Khalaili is progressing.

The Israeli international saw a £21million move to Inter Milan collapse over a medical issue but has had a number of clubs enquiring since.

Khalaili has had his medical ahead of signing a five-year deal.

Charles edges closer to Fulham switch

Shea Charles is undergoing his Fulham medical this morning ahead of his £30million transfer from Southampton.

Fulham have agreed to pay £27m with a further £3m in add-ons for the 22-year-old after Manchester City declined their option to activate matching rights.

Southampton retain a 20 per cent sell-on while Charles has agreed a five-year deal with an option for a further year.

McNeil and Johnson undergo medicals

Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deal to Everton and Crystal Palace.

Brennan Johnson are Dwight McNeil look set to swap their Premier League teams

McNeil nearly joined Palace on Deadline Day in January, but the £20m move broke down due to paperwork not being submitted in time.

Johnson has struggled to settle at Palace since joining from Tottenham for £35m in January. Everton have also held an interest in Johnson in previous windows.

Everton's move for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston looks off as it stands.

Hammers approach Vardy

West Ham are among a number of clubs to have approached free agent Jamie Vardy.

The Hammers see the former England man as an option if they fail to prise Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar.

Vardy, 39, is determined to take his time over his next move as there was a feeling he rushed a family decision to join Cremonese last year despite the value of the experience.

West Ham are one of several clubs monitoring Jamie Vardy

New Fox Franco

The 27-year-old has signed a three-year contract at the King Power.

Blackpool are signing Middlesbrough defender Finley Munroe on loan.

City running rule over Rulli

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is undergoing a medical at Manchester City after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Belgian club Mechelen have agreed a deal to sign Sunderland defender Leo Hjelde.
