World.title: Groups urge Tinubu to reject tobacco control amendment, demand fresh legislative review
World.content:
Civil society and public health organisations have urged President Bola Tinubu to withhold assent to a proposed amendment to Nigeria’s tobacco control law, warning that some provisions could weaken existing safeguards against tobacco and nicotine addiction, particularly among young people.

The groups made the call at a press conference in Abuja on Monday, titled “Why Nigeria Must Reject Harmful Amendments to the National Tobacco Control Act.”

The event was organised by the Nigeria Tobacco Control Alliance (NTCA), in collaboration with Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) and other tobacco control organisations.

Beyond asking Mr Tinubu to withhold assent, the coalition called on the National Assembly to recall the consolidated National Tobacco Control (Amendment) Bill, 2025, and subject it to what it described as a transparent, public health-led review.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The demand followed the Senate’s approval of the bill after its earlier passage by the House of Representatives, bringing the proposed legislation closer to presidential consideration.

‘Reject the bill’

Reading the coalition’s statement, CAPPA Executive Director Akinbode Oluwafemi said the organisations supported updating the National Tobacco Control Act, 2015, and its 2019 regulations to reflect changes in the tobacco and nicotine markets.

He, however, said such changes should not come at the expense of existing public health safeguards.

Mr Oluwafemi acknowledged provisions the coalition considered positive, including the proposed extension of smoke-free zones to within 30 metres of schools and health facilities, and the inclusion of the Nigeria Police Force and the ministry responsible for youth development in the National Tobacco Control Committee.

He argued, however, that these provisions did not outweigh other changes the coalition considered potentially harmful.

The coalition, therefore, urged Mr Tinubu to withhold assent if the bill reaches his desk.

It also asked the National Assembly to publish the committee reports, voting records and stakeholder submissions that informed the consolidated version of the bill.

The groups further called on the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to clarify its position on the legislation and demand its recall if it was not adequately consulted during the legislative process.

Questions over consolidated bill

The Country Coordinator of the Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids (CTFK), Michael Olaniyan, questioned how the consolidated version of the bill was produced, claiming it contained provisions not included in documents presented at the House of Representatives’ public hearing in November 2024.

According to him, the earlier documents totalled four pages, while the consolidated version runs to 31 pages.

“What we have now is a 31-page new document that suddenly emanated from a four-page combined document,” he said.

Mr Olaniyan questioned how the additional provisions were introduced and which public health institutions were consulted before they were incorporated.

Advertising loopholes

Mr Oluwafemi also raised concerns about provisions the coalition said would relax existing restrictions on tobacco advertising, promotion and sponsorship.

He said the bill would permit the promotion of non-combustible products through adult publications, point-of-sale materials, and online platforms, as well as the sponsorship of cultural, social, and recreational events targeted at adults.

He particularly criticised the proposed definition of an “adult publication” as one with a readership of at least 50 per cent adults.

According to him, such a threshold could allow publications with substantial numbers of younger readers to carry s for tobacco and nicotine products.

Smaller packs, weaker enforcement

The Executive Director of A New Thing International Foundation, Kenneth Anetot, said provisions allowing tobacco and nicotine products to be displayed at points of sale and sold in smaller packs could increase their visibility and accessibility among young people.

Mr Anetot said adolescents were particularly vulnerable to addictive substances because their brains were still developing, including areas involved in decision-making and impulse control.

He urged the National Assembly to recall the bill and allow wider stakeholder participation in its review.

READ ALSO: Group warns against tobacco industry still targeting Nigerian youths despite control laws

Nigeria’s tobacco burden

The coalition’s concerns come as tobacco control advocates warn that tobacco use and nicotine addiction continue to impose a significant health and economic burden on Nigeria.

The WHO describes tobacco as a major risk factor for cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, more than 20 types of cancer and other debilitating health conditions. It also states that tobacco kills more than seven million people globally each year.

In Nigeria, the NTCA has previously cited estimates that tobacco-related illnesses cost the country more than N211 billion annually, including healthcare expenses and productivity losses, while nearly 30,000 people died from tobacco-related causes in 2021.

The alliance said young Nigerians were being exposed to smoking, vaping and shisha imagery through music videos, fashion and digital platforms.

A recent study also raised concerns about tobacco marketing targeting women and girls in Nigeria, suggesting that the industry is expanding its marketing strategies to reach new groups of potential consumers.

The health and economic burden of tobacco has also heightened concerns about weakening the safeguards Nigeria has built over the years.

Speaking at Monday’s event, NTCA Coordinator Olawale Makanjuola said Nigeria had made significant progress in tobacco control and argued that some of its regulatory approaches had become reference points for other African countries.

He cited efforts to regulate tobacco imagery in entertainment as one area in which Nigeria had made progress.

Mr Makanjuola warned that provisions in the proposed amendment could reverse some of those gains.

He urged the government and lawmakers to ensure that any changes to the National Tobacco Control Act strengthen, rather than weaken, protections against tobacco and nicotine-related harm.

World.title: Crude supply to local refineries rises 88.4% in Q2 — NUPRC
World.content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

ABUJA — Crude oil and condensate supply to local refineries rose by 88.4 per cent to 53.7 million barrels in the second quarter of 2026, Q2’26, from 28.5 million barrels in the first quarter, Q1’26, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, NUPRC, has said.

The commission, in its Q2 2026 statistics on the enforcement of the Domestic Crude Supply Obligation, DCSO, said the 53.7 million barrels supplied to domestic refiners represented 97.4 per cent performance during the quarter.

The DCSO is being enforced by NUPRC pursuant to Section 109 of the Petroleum Industry Act, PIA, which provides for the supply of crude oil produced in Nigeria to domestic refineries.

According to the commission, the increase in crude supply coincided with higher domestic oil production and the execution of long-term crude supply agreements supported by bankable Sales and Purchase Agreements, SPAs, between producers and domestic refiners.

NUPRC said it conducts monthly consultations with crude oil producers and licensed domestic refineries, following which specific volumes of crude oil and condensate are allocated to producers for supply to local refiners.

It, however, noted that the DCSO operates on a “willing buyer, willing seller” basis in accordance with the PIA, which affects the volumes eventually supplied and accepted.

In April, NUPRC allocated 18.13 million barrels to producers, while producers offered 19.31 million barrels to domestic refiners. Actual supply stood at 20.88 million barrels, representing 114.9 per cent performance against the allocation.

In May, the commission allocated 18.78 million barrels, while producers offered 23.19 million barrels to local refiners. Actual supply fell to 14.23 million barrels, representing 75.8 per cent compliance.

Supply increased in June, with NUPRC allocating 18.17 million barrels to producers, while producers offered 26.84 million barrels to refiners. Actual supply stood at 18.61 million barrels, representing 102.4 per cent performance.

The commission said the figures showed that the DCSO was being actively administered and enforced, adding that the improvement was supported by increased crude production and stronger commercial arrangements between producers and refiners.

At the refinery level, NUPRC said Dangote Refinery required 63 million barrels of crude in Q2, while producers offered 68.1 million barrels.

The 68.1 million barrels offered represented 98 per cent of the total crude volumes offered by producers during the quarter.

However, the refinery accepted 52.6 million barrels, representing 78 per cent of the volume offered to it.

NUPRC said it remained committed to supporting the Federal Government’s objective of achieving energy sufficiency by leveraging the PIA to sustain the growth in crude oil production and continuously enforce the DCSO.

World.title: C’River deputy governor’s convoy crashes, several injured
World.content:
…Odey unhurt — Press Secretary

By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

CALABAR — The convoy of the Cross River State Deputy Governor, Dr Peter Odey, was on Sunday involved in an accident along the Ikom-Calabar highway near Ugep, headquarters of Yakurr Local Government Area of the state.

The incident occurred while the deputy governor and members of his entourage were returning to Calabar from Obanliku Local Government Area, where they had attended an official engagement.

The Press Secretary to the Deputy Governor, Mr Fred Abua, who confirmed the incident to Vanguard, said the press crew vehicle and a Hilux in the convoy were affected.

According to him, the accident occurred after the brakes of the press crew vehicle failed, forcing the driver to veer off the road.

Abua, however, said the vehicle conveying the deputy governor was not directly involved in the accident, adding that Odey was unhurt.

He said: “Only the press crew vehicle and a Hilux were affected. The brakes of the press crew vehicle failed and the driver veered off the road.”

However, several members of the convoy were reportedly injured in the accident.

Another source told Vanguard that the Government House press bus, which was conveying appointees and staff of the Office of the Deputy Governor, veered off its lane near an Army checkpoint in Ugep and rammed into sandbag barricades.

The source also attributed the accident to brake failure, adding that other vehicles in the convoy were damaged.

The extent of the injuries and damage could not be independently verified as of press time.

Efforts to reach other officials for further details were unsuccessful.

World.title: Flight cancelled after child refuses to wear seatbelt, leaves passengers stranded
World.content:
By Mary Agbabiaka

A Porter Airlines flight in Canada was cancelled after a child refused to sit down and fasten their seatbelt, creating unsafe conditions for take-off and forcing the aircraft to return to the gate.

The parent and child were removed from the plane with their luggage, but the disruption meant the flight could not depart as planned.

The incident happened on Thursday at Victoria International Airport in British Columbia, when the Toronto-bound flight was preparing to take off. The aircraft had left the terminal and was heading towards the runway when cabin crew and the child’s parent repeatedly tried to secure the child in their seat.

According to Porter Airlines, the child was standing in their seat and would not remain secured despite several attempts by the parent and crew. The plane was therefore forced to return to the gate so the child and parent could disembark.

The remaining passengers also had to leave the aircraft while the airline refiled its flight plans and completed other paperwork. By the time the process was finished, the delay had pushed the flight beyond the runway’s closure time of 12.30am.

As a result, passengers were left stranded in British Columbia overnight and had to be rebooked on another flight the following day. Porter Airlines apologised for the inconvenience caused.

The airline has not said how old the child was or how many passengers were on the 132-seat aircraft.

Passengers told Canadian broadcaster CBC that there was “a lot of frustration” after the cancellation.

Passenger Aryeh Kozuch said the child did not appear to be behaving badly, but seemed frightened.

“They just kept hiding under their seat,” Kozuch said. “If they got forced into being strapped in, they just kind of slid out underneath.”

Another passenger, Hillary Hertzberg, said it “took forever” for the parent and child to disembark and criticised the airline’s communication following the cancellation.

Some passengers were left scrambling to find hotel rooms nearby and said they wanted the airline to compensate them for the additional expenses caused by the disruption.

World.title: ASUU shuts down IMSU, begins indefinite strike
World.content:
By Emmanuel Iheaka

OWERRI — The Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, Imo State University, IMSU, branch has commenced an indefinite strike over alleged non-payment of salaries, promotion arrears and other entitlements owed its members.

The union announced the commencement of the industrial action on Monday, August 10, 2026, saying the strike would be total and indefinite until its demands are met.

In a statement signed by the branch Chairperson and Secretary, Stephen Oguji and Lazarus Chikwendu, respectively, ASUU said the Federal Government and the union signed an agreement on December 23, 2025, on improved welfare and other conditions of service for academic staff in public universities.

The union alleged that the Imo State Government had failed to implement the agreement at IMSU despite repeated engagements, ultimatums and appeals.

According to the union, implementation of the agreement had commenced in some state-owned universities, including those in Bauchi, Ekiti, Ogun, Osun and Sokoto states.

It said: “While implementation has commenced in some state-owned universities, including those owned by Bauchi, Ekiti, Ogun, Osun and Sokoto states, it is saddening that such has not happened in IMSU despite repeated engagements with our university administration.

“To be sure, before now, the branch, following the directive of the National Executive Council, has formally presented the agreement to the university administration severally, interacted with management and issued a 21-day ultimatum, yet nothing was done.”

ASUU-IMSU also alleged that some of its members were owed several months’ salaries, while promotion arrears dating back to 2016 remained unpaid.

The union further alleged the withholding of 21 months’ check-off dues, non-payment of Earned Academic Allowance, EAA, since 2009, and the continued inclusion of the university in the Treasury Single Account, TSA, which it described as an erosion of university autonomy.

It recalled that the branch embarked on a strike in 2024 over some of the issues but suspended the action following an appeal and assurances from the university management.

“ASUU-IMSU has therefore today, 10th August, 2026 embarked on a total and indefinite strike and vows never to return to work until the agreement is fully implemented,” the union said.

The union urged the Imo State Government to immediately direct the implementation of the 2025 ASUU-FGN agreement at the university, warning that continued delay would heighten industrial tension.

It also appealed to traditional and religious institutions, civil society organisations, parents, student unions and other stakeholders to intervene and prevail on the Visitor to IMSU to address the issues.

ASUU-IMSU, however, said it remained committed to dialogue and constructive engagement, stressing that its willingness to resolve the dispute peacefully should not be interpreted as acceptance of what it described as the continued denial of members’ legitimate welfare rights.

World.title: Alleged IVF Fraud: AGF takes over trial of Abuja Doctor, 2 others
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA— The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, has taken over the prosecution of Abuja-based fertility doctor, John Abebe, accused of fraud and unlawful disclosure of confidential medical records of a patient.

Also cited as 2nd and 3rd defendants in the three-count charge marked CR/005/2026 are Joje Abebe Facility Centre Limited and Balikis Bakare.

According to the FG, the defendants unlawfully revealed the confidential medical records of a patient, Mrs. Mary Manga, without consent, thereby violating her right to medical confidentiality contrary to the provisions of the National Health Act, 2014.

The prosecution further alleged that the 1st defendant breached a confidentiality agreement relating to the reproductive health status of Mrs. Manga’s husband by attaching confidential medical records to a pre-action demand notice issued through his lawyers.

It told the court that the said documents became accessible to third parties, causing emotional trauma to the complainants.

In count three of the charge, it was alleged that the embattled medical doctor had, between January and May 2025, fraudulently obtained N19 million from the complainants by falsely representing himself as an in vitro fertilization (IVF) specialist.

According to the FG, the 1st defendant converted both the money and the embryos extracted from the patients to his personal use, contrary to the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Related Offences Act, 2006.

Though it was the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) that initially filed the charge before a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, the AGF applied to take over the prosecution.

The defendants had since pleaded their innocence to the allegations, even as trial Justice A. A. Fashola, in a ruling on March 11, released them on bail pending the determination of the case.

World.title: Insurance recapitalisation: Oyedele queries NAICOM over fees, escrow funds
World.content:
Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister for the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

ABUJA — The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, has queried the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, over the imposition of a one per cent Capital Injection Fee and other charges on insurance companies undergoing recapitalisation.

The query followed petitions by NICON Insurance Limited and Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation, which challenged the fees and NAICOM’s directive requiring insurers to transfer their entire capital injection funds into an escrow account with the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN.

In a memo referenced F/LEG/0608/2026/22, dated August 6 and signed by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Finance, Mr Raymond Omachi, on behalf of the minister, NAICOM was directed to provide a detailed response and legal justification for the disputed requirements.

The ministry also directed the commission to suspend enforcement of the contested processing fees, one per cent Capital Injection Fee and full capital escrow transfer directive against NICON and Nigeria Re pending the determination of their petitions.

The companies had challenged what they described as additional financial obligations imposed by NAICOM beyond statutory requirements.

They specifically questioned the one per cent Capital Injection Fee, as well as processing and verification fees contained in NAICOM’s Minimum Capital Requirement Guidelines, amounting to N305 million for NICON and N375 million for Nigeria Re.

The two firms also opposed NAICOM’s directive requiring existing and operational insurance companies to transfer their entire capital injection funds into an escrow account at the CBN, arguing that Section 16(3) of the Nigeria Insurance Industry Reform Act, NIIRA, 2025, prescribes a 10 per cent statutory deposit.

NICON and Nigeria Re said they had met the July 31, 2026 recapitalisation deadline by injecting N20 billion and N30 billion respectively into Mudaba Term Deposit Accounts with Lotus Bank Ltd.

According to them, the amounts exceeded their adjusted recapitalisation requirements of N16 billion and N28 billion respectively.

The companies further said they had deposited N2.5 billion each with the CBN pursuant to Section 16(3) of NIIRA 2025 and had made initial fee payments of N80 million and N75 million respectively.

However, NAICOM, in its response yesterday, maintained that the disputed requirements were not new.

“All these are requirements released since last year in the Guidelines which all the recapitalised 43 companies and the eight awaiting verification have complied with,” the commission said.

The development comes amid the ongoing implementation of the federal government’s recapitalisation exercise for the insurance industry, aimed at strengthening the financial capacity and resilience of insurance companies.

World.title: Jonathan, Diri, Ogbuku hail Azikel Group’s industrialisation drive in Bayelsa
World.content:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

YENAGOA — Former First Lady, Dame Patience Jonathan; Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri; and the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, NDDC, Dr Samuel Ogbuku, have commended Azikel Group for its commitment to industrialising Bayelsa State and the Niger Delta region.

The leaders spoke on Monday while inspecting the Crude Distillation Unit, CDU, and other facilities at the Azikel Refinery in Obunagha, Yenagoa Local Government Area of the state.

They also pledged continued support for the successful completion of the multi-billion-naira refinery project.

Representing Governor Diri at the event, his deputy, Dr Peter Akpe, expressed satisfaction with the progress of the project, describing it as a major step towards industrialising the state, creating jobs and opening new economic opportunities for residents.

Akpe congratulated the President of Azikel Group, Dr Azibapu Eruani, and his team on the successful procurement of the CDU, describing the equipment as the most critical component of a refinery and a significant milestone towards completion of the project.

He said industrialisation remained a key component of the Prosperity Administration’s agenda, adding that the government’s responsibility was to create an enabling environment for businesses and investments to thrive.

According to him, the state government’s ongoing road projects were aimed at improving connectivity and providing easier access to industrial investments, including the refinery.

He urged Bayelsans to take advantage of employment and skills-development opportunities that would emerge from the project, while cautioning against commercialising opportunities meant for the people.

He said: “The Prosperity Government, which is the agenda that we propagate, has industry and industrialisation as one of the major things. As a government, our business is to provide or enhance ease of doing business.

“Our universities have got graduates that can fit into most of the levels that will be available.”

Akpe, however, stressed the need for local residents to acquire the necessary skills and capacity to participate meaningfully in the investment.

Also speaking, Dame Patience Jonathan commended the state government for supporting the project, particularly through infrastructure development and improved road access to the refinery.

She said the investment was significant because Bayelsa had traditionally depended heavily on government, stressing that sustainable development required investments capable of creating wealth rather than dependence solely on salaries and statutory allocations.

Dame Jonathan described the refinery as an investment that deserved the collective support of the government, host communities and other stakeholders.

She said: “It is not the amount of money you get at the moment, but the investment you put on ground that matters.”

In his remarks, NDDC Managing Director, Dr Samuel Ogbuku, said the refinery would have a multiplier effect on Bayelsa’s economy through job creation and increased business activities.

Ogbuku said the project could also boost passenger traffic at the Bayelsa International Airport by attracting investors, contractors and other business interests to the state.

He urged Bayelsans, particularly youths, to prepare themselves to benefit from the opportunities that would be created by the investment rather than remain spectators.

The NDDC boss also commended the state government for improving road access to the refinery, saying the infrastructure had made the investment more accessible and demonstrated the government’s preparedness for the economic opportunities associated with the project.

On his part, Eruani described the refinery as a major industrial milestone for Bayelsa State and Nigeria, saying the arrival of the CDU had taken the project to a critical stage.

He disclosed that the refinery, with a capacity of 25,000 barrels per day and an estimated investment value of about $1 billion, would produce petrol, diesel, aviation fuel, kerosene, liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, naphtha and heavy fuel oil.

Eruani said the arrival of the CDU marked the culmination of eight years of work and represented a significant step towards actualising the refinery project.

He explained that the CDU took more than three years to construct in South Korea before it was transported to Nigeria on a specially chartered vessel.

The Chairman of the Bayelsa State Traditional Rulers Council, King Bubaraye Dakolo; former Chief Operating Officer, Refinery and Petrochemical, NNPC, Mr Mustapha Yakubu; and other dignitaries also delivered goodwill messages at the event.

World.title: NDC faction commissions new secretariat in Anambra, passes vote of confidence on leadership
World.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — The factional leadership of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, in Anambra State has commissioned its newly acquired state secretariat in Awka, describing the development as a major step towards strengthening the party’s structure and unity in the state.

The factional state Chairman, Mr Chukwudifu Patrick David, who spoke during the commissioning, assured party members that their contributions to the growth of the party would be recognised and valued.

David said the acquisition of the secretariat was in line with the party’s determination to consolidate its political structure, promote unity and provide a central hub for its activities across the state.

He said: “This is a major step towards consolidating our political structure and fostering party unity in the Anambra State chapter of NDC. It is also to bring together party leaders, stakeholders and grassroots supporters to establish a central hub for party operations across the state.

“I urge every party member to be sincere and faithful to our great party, regardless of the wave we have experienced. I want to remind you that everything that happened is for the benefit of the future of our great party.

“I am not here only to be the chairman, but your loyal and confident servant. Let us move our great party, NDC, as one family. I assure you that my leadership will give a listening ear to any complaint and provide answers and solutions to issues raised.”

The chairman urged members to work together and uphold the party’s ideology, saying internal cohesion and sincerity of purpose were essential to achieving electoral success.

“We can only succeed as one united family if we stand fit, firm and stand by the truth and always do the right thing in our party. We must pay attention to our party ideology and ensure internal cohesion and sincerity of purpose, which is the primary foundation for forthcoming electoral successes,” he said.

The commissioning attracted commendation from representatives of the party’s 21 Local Government Areas in the state.

Speaking on behalf of the 21 LGA chairmen, the NDC Chairman for Oyi Local Government Area, Chief Emmanuel Ifefiora, commended the state leadership for what he described as its effective leadership style.

Ifefiora expressed confidence that the party’s current direction would strengthen its grassroots presence and position it for electoral success across the state’s 21 local government areas.

Also, the NDC Chairman for Anaocha LGA, Mr Nestor Alike, moved a vote of confidence in David’s leadership.

Alike described the establishment of the state secretariat and the expansion of the party’s grassroots mobilisation as significant achievements that would enhance the party’s visibility and stability in the state.

The motion was seconded by the NDC Chairman for Anambra East LGA, Mr Paul Okolo, who reaffirmed the unity of the party under David’s leadership and dismissed claims of internal division.

World.title: 2027: Alli’s Grassroots Support Will Deliver Oyo to APC, Oyewumi Declares
World.content:
Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

A prominent chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State, Prince Oyekunle Oyewumi, has declared that the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Senator Sarafadeen Alli, is strategically positioned to win the governorship election on the strength of his extensive grassroots support across the state.

Oyewumi, a former member of the Board of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), described Alli as an astute public administrator, consummate politician and philanthropist whose political experience, inclusive leadership style and longstanding engagement with the people of the state would give him a competitive advantage in the 2027 contest.

The APC chieftain, in a statement on Monday, said Alli had over the years built a formidable grassroots political network across the nooks and crannies of Oyo State, stressing that his experience and understanding of the state would be valuable in steering its affairs if elected governor.

According to him, Alli’s political pedigree and contributions to the growth and development of Oyo State had demonstrated his capacity to provide purposeful leadership and take the state to greater heights.

Oyewumi, who is also a businessman and Ogbomoso prince, urged APC members and supporters to remain united, calm and committed to the party ahead of the 2027 general election, expressing confidence that the party would emerge victorious.

He also commended Alli for what he described as his inclusive approach to leadership and spirit of sportsmanship, saying the governorship candidate had demonstrated the capacity to accommodate divergent views and build consensus among party members and stakeholders.

Oyewumi equally praised the leadership of the APC in the state for upholding the ideals of the party and promoting unity in its activities, urging members to sustain the momentum as preparations for the 2027 elections gather pace.

He further commended the people of the state for their support for the administration of President Bola Tinubu, saying the Federal Government’s policies under the Renewed Hope Agenda would address some of the structural and economic challenges inherited from previous administrations.

The APC chieftain expressed optimism that the policies and programmes of the Tinubu administration would ultimately translate into improved economic opportunities and better living conditions for Nigerians.

He urged Oyo residents to continue to support the Federal Government, arguing that sustained implementation of its reform agenda would help correct what he described as the anomalies of the past.

Oyewumi maintained that the combination of Alli’s political experience, grassroots acceptance and leadership qualities, alongside the APC’s organisational structure, would place the party in a strong position ahead of the 2027 Oyo State governorship election.

World.title: NOPPMAN Seeks ECOWAS’ Intervention Over Ghana Onion Truck Blockade
World.content:
*Association decries ₦1.2bn losses as Nigerian trucks face continued restrictions, proposes formal MoU under AfCFT

Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria, NOPPMAN, has called on ECOWAS to urgently intervene in the continued restriction of Nigerian and Nigerien onion trucks at Kotoku Market in Ghana.

In a press conference in Sokoto the National President, Alhaji Aliyu Isah Maitasamu, the association said the protracted delays were inflicting huge financial losses on exporters and transporters while exposing highly perishable onions to deterioration.

He said NOPPMAN acknowledged and appreciated the efforts of the Governments of Nigeria and Ghana to resolve the matter. It specifically commended the Honourable Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment of Nigeria and the Deputy Minister of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry of Ghana, as well as diplomats and other stakeholders who have waded into the dispute.

However, Maitasamu stated that despite previous interventions and resolutions reached, Nigerian onion trucks continue to face restrictions in offloading their consignments at Kotoku Market.

He explained that the delays are not only hurting traders but also threatening the stability of cross-border food supply chains between the two West African countries.

The NOPPMAN President stressed that the association’s concern is not with the people or traders of Ghana. He noted that Nigeria and Ghana have longstanding economic, diplomatic and people-to-people relations built on mutual trade and cooperation.

“Our concern is with the unilateral imposition of restrictions on legitimate cross-border trade by market actors, particularly where such restrictions are inconsistent with arrangements previously agreed by relevant stakeholders,” he said.

Maitasamu argued that no market association or group of traders should have the power to unilaterally determine the movement, allocation or offloading of legitimate consignments originating from another ECOWAS Member State.

He therefore called on ECOWAS to act as a neutral mediator and facilitate a lasting solution involving the Governments of Nigeria and Ghana, relevant trade authorities, and onion associations and market stakeholders from both countries.

To forestall future occurrences, NOPPMAN proposed the development of a formal Memorandum of Agreement for cross-border onion trade. The agreement, he said, should be guided by the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme, AfCFTA and other relevant regional mechanisms.

According to him, such an arrangement should establish clear rules on market access, truck movement, offloading, allocation of consignments and dispute resolution, to prevent detention of trucks, deterioration of produce, retaliation or disruption of legitimate trade.

The association said it is seeking a permanent and fair system, and noted that before exportation can resume, there must be a binding memorandum of understanding with exporting countries. Maitasamu disclosed that the impasse has already resulted in estimated losses of N1 billion to Nigerian traders.

World.title: Lai Mohammed, Industry Leaders Back Standardisation at Nigeria Food Summit
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Former Minister of Information and Culture, Alhaji Lai Mohammed, and other industry leaders have called for the standardisation of Nigerian gastronomy, saying the move would strengthen the country’s food systems, promote culinary tourism and position Nigerian cuisine for greater global competitiveness.

The call was made at the recently held Nigeria Food Summit 2026, which was staged at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, with the theme, ‘Gastronomy in Nigeria: Journey to Standardization.’

The two-day summit brought together policymakers, government officials, chefs, restaurateurs, hospitality professionals, entrepreneurs, researchers, investors, regulators, development partners, students and other stakeholders in Nigeria’s food value chain.

Mohammed, who is Special Adviser to the Secretary-General of UN Tourism and Chairman of the Board of Trustees and Governing Council of the Eko Tourism Foundation, delivered a keynote address titled, ‘Building Nigeria’s Food System: Standardizing Gastronomy for Power and Prosperity’.

He said Nigerian cuisine should be regarded not only as cultural heritage but also as an economic asset capable of driving tourism, exports, investment and national development.

“Standardizing Nigerian gastronomy is not a cosmetic exercise – it is nation-building work,” he said, urging stakeholders to develop systems that would protect quality, authenticity and Nigeria’s culinary heritage.

“Countries that succeed globally document, protect, regulate and intentionally promote their cuisine. Nigeria has every reason to stand alongside them,” he said.

“By building systems that protect quality, authenticity and our culinary heritage, we can transform Nigerian food into a powerful instrument of economic growth, cultural diplomacy and global competitiveness,” he added.

The Convener of the Nigeria Food Summit and chef, Captain Gbolabo Gibbs Adebakin, also called for the discussions at the summit to translate into practical action.

Adebakin, in his welcome address, said standardisation should move beyond an aspiration to become an industry-wide practice, requiring collaboration among government, businesses, educational institutions, hospitality operators and other stakeholders.

“The conversations we have had over these two days must now become commitments. Standardization cannot remain an aspiration – it must become our collective practice,” he said.

“Building a globally respected Nigerian gastronomy industry requires collaboration across government, business, education, hospitality and every stakeholder in the food value chain. This summit is only the beginning.”

The summit attracted nearly 1,000 participants and recorded close to 800 ticket sales. More than 300 speakers, moderators and panelists participated in the programme, alongside about 200 VIP guests, 30 sponsors and strategic partners, and nearly 20 exhibitors.

Among those who participated were the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Agriculture and Food Systems, Emmanuel Fatai Audu; Lagos State Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Systems, Abisola Olusanya; Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of PricePally, Jummai Abalaka; NFS26 Culinary Director, Chef TYB; Hilda Baci; Chef Eros; Oyinbo Olonje; Chude Jideonwo; Alhaja Abraham Oyinkansola of Honeycraft Foodies; Lucky Idike; and Group Head, Agric and Solid Minerals Finance, Sterling Bank, Dr. Shola Obikanye.

The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) was also represented at the summit, with Ms Nene Obianwu participating in a policy panel alongside government and industry stakeholders.

Industry associations, including CAPA, RCBC, FTAN, APCN, APFSPN and REFSPAN, as well as the Slow Food Cooks’ Alliance Nigeria and other culinary and hospitality groups, also participated in the discussions.

The summit also provided opportunities for networking, business matchmaking and cross-sector engagement, while an exhibition showcased food brands, agricultural enterprises, technology-driven solutions and hospitality businesses to consumers, investors, policymakers and potential partners.

The event was backed by a number of organisations across the banking, agriculture, food, hospitality and communications sectors.

The organisers said the Nigeria Food Summit would continue to pursue dialogue, partnerships, research and policy engagement aimed at accelerating the standardisation and global recognition of Nigerian gastronomy.

World.title: Plateau: One-Term Pledge Can’t Replace Devt Plan, PGID Tells Kefiano
World.content:
The Plateau Initiative for Growth and Development has urged the Peoples Democratic Party governorship candidate, Chief Kefas Ropshik Kefiano, to present a detailed development agenda instead of centring his campaign on a pledge to serve only one term.

PIGD made the call in a Monday statement by its National Coordinator, Nengak David, who said the pledge raised questions about the candidate’s priorities and campaign commitments built around zoning.

According to the group, Plateau voters deserve explanations of how Kefiano intends to address insecurity, unemployment, infrastructure, agriculture, education and healthcare.

“The people need to hear what Chief Kefiano will do with power, not merely how long he says he will hold it,” David said. “A one-term pledge cannot substitute for a practical programme showing how the state will be governed and developed.”

PIGD urged Kefiano to explain policies, timelines and measurable targets, allowing voters to assess him on competence and character rather than zonal sentiment.

The organisation also questioned why the electorate should accept the pledge without scrutiny, drawing a comparison with Kefiano’s career in business.

“Chief Kefiano is a businessman who has never publicly declared that he intends to stop making money,” the statement said. “Why, then, should Plateau citizens simply believe that a politician who wins power will willingly surrender it after one term? Such a promise requires more than words; it requires convincing guarantees and demonstrable sincerity.”

The group stressed that its intervention was not directed solely at Kefiano or the PDP, but at candidates and parties across Plateau State.

“We call on politicians, irrespective of party affiliation, to speak honestly to the people,” David said. “Campaigns must be driven by truth, realistic promises and a genuine commitment to service. Plateau has suffered enough from convenient declarations that disappear once elections are over.”

PIGD advised residents to interrogate campaign pledges and demand issue-based engagements from candidates ahead of the election.

“Democracy becomes stronger when citizens refuse to be carried away by sentiment,” it added. “Every candidate must tell Plateau people what will be done, how it will be done and how the public can hold the government accountable.”

World.title: Revenue Monitoring Group Lauds Customs For Bold Reforms in Trade, Security, Technology
World.content:
The Revenue Monitoring Group of Nigeria (RMGN) has commended the Nigeria Customs Service, (NCS) for what it described as “a strategic transformation” in trade facilitation, border security and technology adoption under the leadership of Comptroller-General, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Monday, the civil society organization said the reforms have repositioned Customs beyond revenue collection to become a key driver of national development.

Signed by RMGN President, Dr. Ifeanyi Duruaku, and Secretary General, Comrade Tor Lumun, the group noted that NCS had successfully ditched age-long manual processes in favour of digital, intelligence-led operations.

“The CGC has redefined NCS processes through automation, transparency, and trust with compliant traders,” RMGN stated. “This has fired up operational capacity and unleashed efficiency across the Service.”

The group specifically highlighted the deployment of the Unified Customs Management System, UCMS, and the B’Odogwu platform, which it said have cut human interference, reduced leakages, and sped up cargo clearance.

RMGN also lauded NCS for strengthening collaboration with the Army, Navy, DSS, EFCC and NFIU to combat smuggling, illicit financial flows, and wildlife trafficking.

On global recognition, the group congratulated Dr. Adeniyi on receiving commendation from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu during the 147th/148th sessions of the World Customs Organisation, WCO Council in Brussels on July 3, 2026, where he was unanimously re-elected as Chairperson.

Quoting the President, RMGN stated:

“Adeniyi’s unanimous re-election is not only a personal honour, but also a recognition of Nigeria’s growing influence in global Customs administration. His leadership has been marked by bold initiatives that have improved revenue generation, strengthened border security, facilitated legitimate trade, and modernised Customs operations through homegrown innovations.

“RMGN described the presidential endorsement as “a glowing testament” to the CGC’s achievements.

Reviewing the last three years, the group said the reforms have delivered visible dividends. It cited 2025 trade figures of ₦194.94 trillion, with exports growing by 219.5% to ₦136.65 trillion, attributing the growth to reform and efficiency, not duty hikes.

“In what amounts to a referendum on the current leadership, it is clear that under Dr. Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, the Nigeria Customs Service has been significantly transformed,” RMGN concluded. “We now have a Service that is delivering on revenue, smarter trade facilitation, more effective anti-smuggling operations, and result-driven environmental protection.”

World.title: EU Denies Rejecting INEC Invitation, Confirms Electoral Expert Mission for 2027 Polls
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The European Union (EU) Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS has dismissed reports that it rejected an invitation from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to observe Nigeria’s 2027 general election, describing the reports as inaccurate and speculative.

The EU, in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday, said it had received a formal invitation from INEC dated April 17, 2026, to deploy observers for the 2027 elections.

Contrary to reports that the EU had declined the invitation citing worsening insecurity and alleged hostile treatment of its observers and officials following the publication of its final report on the 2023 general election, the delegation said it had accepted the invitation and would deploy an Electoral Expert Mission (EEM).

It said the response to INEC, dated July 28, 2026, thanked the electoral commission for the invitation and informed it that the EU would field an EEM comprising between two and four independent experts, who would be formally accredited as observers by INEC.

The delegation stressed that the two reasons attributed to the EU in the reports did not appear in its letter to INEC.

“The two alleged reasons mentioned in the press reports do not appear in the letter: these are pure speculations,” the EU said.

According to the delegation, an EEM, like an Electoral Observation Mission, assesses whether an electoral process is conducted in line with international, regional and national obligations and commitments on democratic elections to which the country has subscribed.

The mission will also submit a final report containing recommendations on improving Nigeria’s electoral framework and future electoral processes.

The EU said the report would be shared with the Nigerian government and could subsequently be made available to the wider public if the government agreed.

Explaining its decision to deploy an expert mission rather than a larger electoral observation mission, the delegation said the EU makes decisions annually on electoral missions to partner countries that invite it, with the type of mission determined by the circumstances of each country and the resources available.

“It is on this basis that the decision to conduct an EEM in Nigeria has been taken and will be further consulted with the relevant Nigerian authorities for its implementation,” it stated.

The clarification comes amid growing preparations for the 2027 general election and heightened public interest in the role international partners will play in monitoring Nigeria’s electoral process.

The EU also rejected any suggestion that its decision to deploy an EEM represented a withdrawal of support for democratic governance or Nigeria’s electoral process.

It said the decision “does not affect in any way” the continued implementation of its EU-funded Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria project, including its support for the electoral process.

The delegation further urged members of the media to verify reports concerning the EU’s positions and statements directly with its press and communication office before publication.

“The EU Delegation respectfully reminds members of the esteemed media community that, to avoid issuing such misleading information about positions or statements of the EU, they can simply check their accuracy with the press and communication office of the EU Delegation,” it said.

The statement, which was signed by the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, effectively puts to rest reports that the EU had turned down INEC’s invitation to participate in the 2027 electoral process, while confirming that the bloc intends to maintain an independent expert presence during the elections.

World.title: Mastercard Announces New Lead for Eastern Europe, Middle East, Africa region
World.content:
Mastercard has announced that Yasemin Bedir has been appointed President of the company’s Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa (EEMEA) region, effective 1 September. The company’s EEMEA region was expanded in recent years, bringing additional markets to what is now a vibrant, agile and high growth potential 81 country business.

Bedir, a nearly 20-year veteran of Mastercard, also joins the company’s Management Committee. She succeeds Dimitrios Dosis, who was recently named Chief Commercial Payments Officer, leading Commercial & New Payment Flows.

In this UAE-based role, Bedir will oversee the strategy, direction and overall success of all aspects of Mastercard’s operations across the region through its partnerships with retailers, fintechs, financial institutions, governments and businesses.

“Yasemin is a leader who finds the best in her teams to help them deliver the greatest impact for our customers and to fuel local economies,” said Sachin Mehra, Chief Business Officer, Mastercard. “This is a vast and complex region that demands creative thinking, proven results and strong relationships. Yasemin has delivered that throughout her career. Working with our customers and partners across the EEMEA region, we have a true opportunity to shape and redefine how people and businesses move money, exchange value and enable commerce for years to come.”

Most recently, Bedir served as Division President for Eastern Europe for four years, guiding the team through a complex geopolitical and regulatory environment to strengthen Mastercard’s leadership position across these markets. She is a passionate advocate for talent development and has fostered a culture grounded in accountability and collaboration.

Bedir joined Mastercard in 2007. During her tenure, she gained experience and insights from working in markets across the globe, including serving as General Manager of the company’s Turkey and Azerbaijan activities before overseeing community institution and processor relationships in North America for nearly five years.

“I’ve been inspired by the teams here at Mastercard,” said Bedir. “Their resilience, innovative spirit and relentless dedication to meet and exceed customer needs is what powers our impact every day. Together, we will build on the strong foundation the regional team has created under Dimi’s leadership over the past five years.”

Earlier in her career, Bedir worked at HSBC, Garanti Bank and Yapı Kredi in Turkey. She is among the Founders of the Professional Women Network (PWN) and leads many projects to help SMEs grow.

World.title: Troops Foil ISWAP Attack on FOB Gajiram, Eliminate Extremist Fighters
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

Troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have foiled an attack by Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists on a Forward Operating Base (FOB) in Gajiram, Nganzai Local Government Area of Borno State, the military said.

According to a statement by the Acting Military Information Officer of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, a large number of terrorists launched an assault in an attempt to overrun the troops’ position at about 12:20 a.m. on 10 August 2026.

This is not the first time Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) extremists have attempted to overrun military facilities across the North-East theatre of operations.

Meanwhile, troops have continued to frustrate such attempts, inflicting heavy casualties and recovering weapons from the insurgents.

The Nigerian military has been battling the insurgency for more than a decade and a half.

The statement noted that the gallant troops responded with determined and effective fire, forcing the attackers to withdraw after sustaining heavy casualties.

During the engagement, troops neutralised several terrorists and recovered weapons, ammunition and communication gadgets.

“Post-engagement review of the surveillance footage further confirmed several casualties being evacuated by the retreating terrorists. The recovered items and footage are currently undergoing further operational assessment,” Captain Goni said.

He, however, regretted that a few troops sustained injuries during the engagement after part of the defences was temporarily breached, leading to damage to some combat-enabling equipment and vehicles from rocket-propelled grenade fire.

The injured personnel were promptly airlifted and are currently stable and receiving medical attention.

Captain Goni said: “Following the attack, troops have remained firmly deployed in and around the FOB and adjoining areas to dominate the general area, monitor the situation and prevent any further attempts by the terrorists to re-engage.

“Residents of Gajiram and surrounding communities are advised to remain calm and go about their lawful activities. Members of the public are also encouraged to promptly report any suspicious movement or activity to the nearest security agencies to support intelligence sharing in the ongoing operations.”

Captain Goni said troops would continue to maintain a high level of vigilance in and around Gajiram, while the exploitation of the operational area and further assessment of the terrorists’ casualties and activities remained ongoing.

“Headquarters Theatre Command, Operation Hadin Kai, reassures the public of its unshakable commitment to sustaining pressure on the ISWAP terrorists until lasting peace and stability are fully restored in the North-East,” he concluded.

World.title: ‘Faced a brutal battle’: Danny K’s wife praised over strength, bravery
World.content:
Lisa Koppel, the wife of Danny Koppel, fondly known as R&B singer Danny K, has been praised for her brave fight against an illness that took her life over the weekend.

The 41-year-old model-turned-lawyer, whose father is well-known mega-attorney Billy Gundelfinger, leaves behind her spouse and their three children.

DANNY K’S WIFE REMEMBERED FOR BRAVE FIGHT

In an emotional Instagram post, Lisa Koppel’s sister Justine Gundelfinger paid tribute to her sibling.



Justine – an actress – revealed that Lisa had passed on Women’s Day – on Sunday, 9 August. Lisa was remembered as a successful supermodel, lawyer and businesswoman.

She shared: “My magical Princess Angel Lillie [her nickname] had the purest and kindest heart. She was stunning, delicate, gentle and soft like a petal. Yet carried within her a strength beyond measure and the remarkable ability to endure even the greatest of storms. Her selfless, down-to-earth, gentle nature, witty sense of humour, brilliant mind, and unconditional love and devotion to her husband, Danny [K], their children, our family and her friends made her truly extraordinary.

Danny K and his wife Lisa Koppel.

Images via Facebook.

Images via Instagram

“She was very hardworking, caring, generous, altruistic and remarkably modest. She was utterly devoted to those she loved and had the incredible gift of making everyone around her feel valued and cared for. Her magnificent children, Jayden, Kyle and Chloe and her husband were the centre of her universe. The boundless love, strength, kindness, patience, and good values she gave them will live within them forever and remain among the greatest expressions of her legacy.



Justine revealed that Lisa Koppel had died after a brave battle with an illness.

She continued: “When Lisa faced the most brutal battle imaginable, she fought with such fortitude, powerful determination, extraordinary courage and phenomenal heroism. She was truly the bravest and strongest woman I have ever known. Her resilience was beyond comprehension. I will forever be in awe of the strength with which she faced even the greatest adversity.

“There is something deeply poignant about honouring Lisa on Women’s Day because to me, she embodied everything extraordinary about being a woman. We mourn her, but we also celebrate her beautiful life, her humour, her generous spirit, her incredible style, grace and elegance, her devotion to her family, and the immense love she gave so freely. 

“You are, and always will be, the woman I aspire to be. I love you beyond infinity”

SINGER’S BEST FRIEND AND SOULMATE

Danny K married Lisa Koppel (née Gundelfinger), whom he has described as his “best friend” and “soulmate,” in 2012 at the Lourensford Wine Estate in Somerset West, Western Cape.



The couple started dating in 2010, shortly after his engagement to ex, Lee-Ann Liebenberg, ended.

Coincidentally, Lee-Ann dated and is now married to businessman Nicky van der Walt, who dated Lisa around the same time as her own relationship with the singer.

Danny K told the Sunday Times in 2020: “It wasn’t an orchestrated swap. It is simply convenient because we both landed up with the people we were meant to be with.”



He continued: “When I look at my kids, and my life, I couldn’t imagine it any other way.”

World.title: RIP | Danny K’s wife Lisa Koppel dies aged 41
World.content:
South African singer Danny K is mourning the death of his wife, Lisa Koppel, with the family asking for privacy following her passing. Image: ChatGPT

South African singer Danny K is mourning the death of his wife, Lisa Koppel, with the family asking for privacy following her passing.

The news was confirmed on Monday by Danny K’s mother, Pam Koppel.

She indicated that the family would not be issuing a formal public statement and that the circumstances surrounding Lisa’s death would remain private.



RIP | Four school learners died this week – South Africa mourns

Deeply saddened by the passing of Lisa Gundelfinger, wife of Danny K.



Our heartfelt thoughts and condolences go out to Danny, their children, and the entire Gundelfinger and Koppel families during this incredibly difficult time.



May Lisa’s memory be a blessing, and may her… pic.twitter.com/fQp88isDuL — Yusuf Abramjee (@Abramjee) August 10, 2026

A life beyond the spotlight

Lisa, the daughter of prominent divorce attorney Billy Gundelfinger, began her career as a model before moving into the legal profession.

She was admitted as an advocate of the High Court in 2010 and went on to build a career in law.

Lisa and Danny K married in 2012 and shared three children.

While Danny K has enjoyed a long and successful career in the South African music industry, Lisa largely maintained a lower public profile, balancing her professional career with family life.



Family tragedy

Lisa’s death is another devastating loss for the Koppel family.

Danny K has previously spoken about the profound impact of losing his brother, Jarren, who died in a helicopter crash in 2003.

Danny K, a multiple South African Music Award winner, has remained one of South Africa’s best-known entertainers since rising to prominence in the early 2000s.

Poem

His father, Gavin Koppel, also appeared to reflect on grief in a poem titled My Promise, which he on Sunday, 9 August.

In the emotional poem, he wrote about turning pain into compassion and vowed: “I will use my pain to heal from this day forward.”

Although Gavin did not explicitly refer to Lisa or confirm her death, the post appeared as news of the family’s loss emerged.

Tributes and messages of condolence have since begun circulating as friends, colleagues and members of the public remember Lisa.

The family has asked for privacy as they mourn her death and support her three children through the difficult period.

World.title: Where pensioners can get private healthcare for free
World.content:
Getting healthcare is either an expensive process or a whole-day event.

Pensioners have a choice between sitting in long queues at a government clinic or paying R650 for a checkup at a local doctor.

That isn’t the case at one private healthcare provider, where pensioners can book an appointment for free.



Free Private Health Care

Clicks launched its Helping Hand Trust in 2011 in partnership with the Western Cape Department of Health (WCDH).

At the time, the initiative was intended to offer baby education, healthcare advice, and basic clinic services to young mothers.

Since then, it has spread nationwide. The service has also expanded.

Now, select Clicks pharmacies offer free basic clinic services on Wednesdays.

To qualify for the free service, pensioners must not have medical aid.

If they do, they will be charged through their medical aid.



Typically, the cost for this service ranges from R120 to R350 depending on the reason for the visit.

On Wednesdays, pensioners can visit a Clicks with a clinic and get a basic checkup for heart health or diabetes.

During these health screenings, the Clicks nurse will check cholesterol levels, measure blood pressure, conduct a glucose test, and offer healthcare advice.

Other free services offered by the retailer include HIV testing and counselling.

Select Clicks’ clinics also offer pap smears, breast exams, and non-invasive prostate screening, but these come at an additional cost.

Booking a Free Clinic Appointment

If your local Clicks has a clinic, you can wait in the queue from 08:00 to 17:00 on Wednesdays.

However, to skip the queue, you can book an appointment online by visiting the Clicks website.

When booking an appointment, you need to select the services with “Helping Hand” in the title.

It’s possible to make an appointment for up to four people. Confirmation will be sent via sms and email.

Pensioners can also book their Helping Hand appointment by dialling the retailer’s customer service line.

Affordable Private Healthcare for Pensioners

Pensioners who want affordable private healthcare through their medical aid can also use Clicks.

The retailer offers premium clinic services between Monday and Friday.

In addition to the heart health and diabetes screening, Clicks offers:

Flu vaccinations

Pneumonia vaccination

Vitamin injections

They also have a nurse-assisted virtual doctor consultation.

During these sessions, the doctor guides the consultation, and the nurse will assist.

Dischem offers similar services.

Dischem nurses provide basic clinic services, but they can also lead a virtual doctor appointment.

These consultations are roughly 45% cheaper than an in-person consultation at a local doctor.

World.title: Two weeks later: Search continues for missing Cape Town siblings
World.content:
Two weeks after they went missing, police say the search for Elsies River siblings Perez, Atarah and Alessia Khumalo continues. Image: The Pink Ladies

Two weeks on, three Elsies River children remain missing as police press on with the search to bring them home.

Alessia Khumalo, 7, Perez Khumalo, 4, and one-year-old Atarah Khumalo were last seen at their Bestenbier Avenue home on 27 July. It’s alleged they left with their dad to get ice-cream at around 12:00 on the day.

Western Cape police have confirmed that the search remains active.



No breakthrough yet

Police spokesperson Captain FC van Wyk said detectives are still working to trace the children.

“The matter you are referring to is still under investigation. The search and investigations continue,” Van Wyk said.

No arrests have been announced.

Police previously confirmed that the siblings were last seen with a man identified as their father. He has not been publicly named as a suspect.

What the siblings were wearing

When they were last seen, Alessia was wearing a blue-and-yellow tracksuit with black shoes. Atarah was dressed in a pink tracksuit and pink shoes, while Perez was wearing a grey tracksuit with black tekkies.

Community appeal continues

The disappearance has left the Elsies River community searching for answers. Missing-persons organisations and residents have continued to circulate appeals for information.



Earlier this week, missing persons organisation The Pink Ladies also appealed to the public for help to find the children after issuing a missing persons alert.

Police urge anyone who may have seen the children or has information about their whereabouts to come forward.

Information can be shared anonymously through Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or via the MySAPS App.

The South African Weather Service has issued an Orange Level 6 warning for disruptive snow, with parts of the Eastern Cape and Free State among the hardest hit.

Eastern Cape authorities said a total of five mountain passes in the high-lying areas of the Eastern Cape remain closed to traffic as snowfall continues to affect parts of the province.

* Barkly Pass – R58 between Ekhephini (Barkly East) and Khowa (Elliot)

World.title: What next for beleaguered FIFA president Infantino?
World.content:
PARIS - Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino's hope that a combative statement condemning "a concerted and ongoing effort" to undermine him would spark a period of reflection were dashed on Monday.

It is over a week since Infantino withdrew his plan to raise private investment for a new commercial subsidiary, called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which it proposed would run the commercial side of World Cups.

Three confederations, Europe's UEFA, North and Central America CONCACAF and Asia's AFC, did not hold back in targetting Infantino and his style of leadership in an open letter on Monday.

Despite all sides calling for unity, their idea of how that can be achieved diverges markedly.

World.title: 'Policemen are on the payroll of the gangsters' - Reiger Park community leader
World.content:
BOKSBURG - Reiger Park EMS Chaplain Eddy Walkerley has accused some police officers of colluding with gangs in the area.

Four people were killed in a shooting on Friday night in Reiger Park, East of Johannesburg.

Two Anti-Gang Unit officers are among those dead.

Walkerley claimed some officers are on gangsters' payroll and are protecting criminals.

"We know the gangsters, we know names. But there are people that know where they stay, there's people that know their faces.

“The people are living in fear, because should you go to the police, the local police, you will be the next target, no matter what.

“Our police are working with a lot of the gangsters. A lot of the policemen are on the payroll of the gangsters, and I'm not afraid to say it. I will say it and I'll even say it in their faces.

“I said it on Friday evening, whilst on the crime scene, I mentioned it, and I'm going to say it again, our police must get out of the pockets of gangsters."

World.title: UK radio broke rules in announcing king's death: watchdog
World.content:
LONDON - A community radio station breached the rules after accidentally announcing the death of King Charles III in a May broadcast, a UK watchdog said on Monday.

Radio Caroline, a former pirate radio that now mostly plays rock music, apologised in May after airing messages falsely announcing the monarch's death.

One of the messages had said "we have suspended our normal programmes until further notice as a mark of respect following the passing of His Majesty King Charles III".

The national anthem was then played, followed by around 16 minutes of silence before the regular programme resumed.

The presenter apologised 30 minutes after the messages were initially triggered, Ofcom said.

The regulator, which received two complaints about the broadcast, said the "very significant inaccuracy" and the "considerable length of time" taken to acknowledge the error breached two of its rules.

One requires news reports to be accurate and impartial.

The other requires significant mistakes to be acknowledged and corrected on air promptly.

Radio Caroline told Ofcom the error occurred when a member of staff accessed sound files pre-recorded in the event of the monarch's death while carrying out maintenance on the studio computer, as the programme was being streamed remotely.

The staff member played the files "out of curiosity", which stopped the stream from the presenter's remote location and broadcast the files on air.

The person then reportedly "panicked and left the premises" after realising what had happened, according to the Ofcom statement.

Radio Caroline said the remote presenter "would not realise that they had gone 'off air' unless they were monitoring their output via an internet monitor."

The presenter, believing they were still on air, was not actively monitoring their phone and did not immediately respond to calls from people at the station who had noticed the error, the report said.

The station said the person who played the files had been "reprimanded" and had "apologised".

It added the pre-recorded files had now been removed from the studio computer.

World.title: Reiger Park Shooting | Person of interest taken in for questioning
World.content:
BOKSBURG – An alleged gang member has been taken in for questioning in connection with the multiple murders that took place in Reiger Park on Friday.

Two police officers part of the Anti-Gang Unit were responding to the shooting of two civilians when they were ambushed.

Acting Police Minister Firoz told fellow officers, family members and the community at large that the state would deploy all the necessary resources needed to bring the culprits to book.

On Monday morning, two R5 rifles linked to the killings were recovered near Germiston.

In a media briefing held with Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi, Cachalia said a person of interest had been taken in.

“One person has been tken in for questioning. But he is not the only person of interest. These murders were not committed by one person,” he said.

He said the person of interest is a known gang member who is currently out on bail and facing six other charges.

Lesufi said “at least now we know who we are looking for.”

At the weekend, authorities visited the families of the slain officers. The funerals of the officers will be held on Saturday and Sunday, respectively.

Cachalia said he has not visited the families of the two civilians because investigations are still ongoing.

World.title: New German transport chief gets taste of train chaos
World.content:
BERLIN - Germany's new transport minister experienced firsthand Monday the problems plaguing the country's rail network, being forced to change train carriages during a trip after the air conditioning broke down.

Steffen Bilger was named to the post in a cabinet shuffle last month after his predecessor was sacked by Chancellor Friedrich Merz for insufficient progress on overhauling Germany's dilapidated infrastructure.

A key part of his role is turning around state-owned operator Deutsche Bahn and the rail network, which has faced mounting complaints in recent years due to dismal punctuality, breakdowns and poor service.

On a two-day trip, Bilger plans to gather information in northern Germany on train safety and station cleanliness.

But at the start of the journey, he had to change carriages in a train taking him from Berlin to Hamburg after the air conditioning stopped working, a transport ministry spokesman told AFP.

The breakdown, which came as Germany bakes in soaring summer temperatures, led to the carriage being closed off and forced passengers to find seats elsewhere on the train.

At the weekend, Bilger reportedly announced that bonus payments for Deutsche Bahn managers would be tied to targets set by the government, including on punctuality.

World.title: Bezos consortium nears deal to buy Liverpool stake: report
World.content:
LONDON - Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is part of a consortium nearing a deal to buy a one-third stake in Premier League club Liverpool, a report said Monday.

Sky News said Bezos was part of an investor group led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of India steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, that also also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed the approach from Bhatia's group last month.

"An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club," an FSG spokesman told AFP.

Bhatia was until recently a shareholder in Championship club Queens Park Rangers.

The Sky report said the consortium was "closing in on a deal to buy a roughly one-third stake in Liverpool", with FSG preparing to make an announcement "as soon as this week".

Bezos, 62, is one of the world's richest men, with a fortune estimated by Forbes magazine at more than $280 billion, while Saverin's wealth is put at $33 billion.

Bezos has reportedly explored previous bids for the NFL's Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders, but decided against pursuing either deal.

Sky said the investment in Liverpool, part of an influx of American money into the Premier League, would reportedly value the 20-time English league champions at $6 billion.

FSG, which also owns the Boston Red Sox baseball team, bought Liverpool in 2010 for £300 million ($405 million).

It sold a minority stake in the club in 2023 to US private equity group Dynasty Equity.

Liverpool won the Premier League title in 2024/25 under Arne Slot but the Dutchman was sacked in May after a turbulent season.

World.title: MEC Maile calls on communities to help protect Gauteng schools
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng Education MEC Lebogang Maile has said protecting schools is a shared responsibility.

Maile briefed the media on plans to curb issues affecting Gauteng schools.

He said issues around bullying, gender-based violence and gangsterism have been of great concern.

The department has embarked on a campaign called - it takes a village to raise a child.

“Violence, gangsterism, bullying, substance abuse, gender-based violence, vandalism and criminal activity around schools were repeatedly raised. The program of action strengthened Safe Schools intervention and cooperation with SAPs, community policing forums, NGOs and communities.

“Work is also being driven on anti-bullying interventions and misconduct measures while school safety matters are being assigned to the responsible education support and curriculum functions.

“The purpose is to move from responding only after incidents occur to prevention, early intervention, clear escalation and coordinated action around high-risk schools. Communities themselves remain essential to the solution. Protecting a school cannot be left entirely to government.

“The communities must help identify criminal activity, protect public infrastructure, support learner discipline and refuse to normalize drug dealing, vandalism and violence around schools."

World.title: Wamboka: Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang'i should back Sifuna
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kabuchai Mp Majimbo kalasinga and his counterpart Jack Wamboka during a press briefing on Monday. [Juliet Omelo, Standard]

The political battle for the 2027 presidency has intensified, with leaders allied to the Linda Mwananchi movement urging opposition figures Kalonzo Musyoka, Rigathi Gachagua and Fred Matiang’i to abandon their presidential ambitions and back Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna.

Bumula MP Jack Wamboka made the call after a three-day political tour of Western Kenya by the Linda mwananchi brigade, saying the region had demonstrated growing grassroots support for Sifuna.

Wamboka said the tour was a major success, with close to 22 rallies held in three days. He added that the crowds reflected growing enthusiasm for Sifuna, particularly among young people, women, political aspirants and ordinary voters.

“We respect you, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i. We know you have what it takes but in 2027, we ask you to stand with Sifuna,” Wamboka said.

He said the reception in Western Kenya showed that Sifuna’s campaign was gaining national attention.

The first time MP said Sifuna had focused on issues affecting Western Kenya, particularly the collapse of industries and the struggling sugar sector. He pointed to Mumias and Nzoia sugar factories, saying their decline had left farmers and workers suffering.

Wamboka accused National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula of failing to deliver development promises made to Bungoma residents citing unfinished roads and the stalled Bungoma stadium, saying several projects lacked adequate funding despite repeated commitments to voters during the campaigns.

He also questioned Wetang’ula’s political record, citing past controversies and accusing the Speaker of failing to live up to his promises adding that voters should judge leaders by what they deliver, not by speeches alone.

Kabuchai MP Majimbo Kalasinga said the tour had proved that Sifuna’s bid was gaining grassroots support.

“Edwin Sifuna is going for president, nothing else,” he said.

He said supporters contributed small amounts to the campaign, arguing that the movement was being funded by ordinary Kenyans rather than wealthy political backers. He said crowds turned up voluntarily.

Kalasinga also announced that Linda Mwananchi would hold a rally in Homa Bay on August 16 despite local warnings. He said Sifuna had a right to campaign anywhere in Kenya.

He called for peaceful competition and warned against attempts to block the rally or restrict political activity in the region emphasising that Kenya is for everyone, constitutionally, peacefully and equally.

They two vowed to fight for the Linda Mwananchi name.

The Wamboka-Kalasinga push adds momentum to Sifuna’s campaign and pressures opposition leaders to unite before the 2027 election.

World.title: Kindiki defends government's development agenda in Mt Kenya
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki and Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on August 10, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reiterated the government’s commitment to ensure equitable development.

Prof Kindiki said that President William Ruto’s government has initiated many development projects in Mt Kenya to transform livelihoods.

“Am advising the people against being deceived to leave the government to join the opposition where nothing is being provided,” he said.

The Deputy President said the road projects which had stalled have since been revived after the government released Sh176 billion owed to contractors to ensure completion of 6,000km.

He spoke at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on Sunday, where he was the chief guest during celebrations to mark 100 years since the establishment of Gaichanjiru Mission Hospital managed by the Catholic Diocese of Murang'a.
